items.name: Allocator
items.comment:
Allocator is the interface that represent any kind of allocator type
             (Permanent, Arena, HeapPages, etc). User must call Allocator.alloc_fn to
             communicate with the real allocator
items.summary: Allocator is the interface that represent any kind of allocator type (Permanent, Arena, HeapPages, etc). User must call Allocator.alloc_fn to communicate with the real allocator

items.name: allocate
items.comment:
Allocates a raw block of memory through the allocator's concrete policy.

Parameters:
  self : ^Allocator - allocator used to reserve the storage.
  size : i64        - requested size in bytes.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - allocated storage and operation status.
items.summary: Allocates a raw block of memory through the allocator's concrete policy.

items.name: allocate_aligned
items.signature: allocate_aligned : func(self : ^Allocator, size : i64, alignment : i64 ) -> [RawPtr, MemoryStatus]
items.comment:
Requests a raw block of memory with the requested alignment.

Parameters:
  self      : ^Allocator - allocator used to reserve the storage.
  size      : i64        - requested size in bytes.
  alignment : i64        - requested byte alignment.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - allocated storage and operation status.

Notes:
  - Alignment behavior is defined by the allocator's concrete policy.
items.summary: Requests a raw block of memory with the requested alignment.

items.name: clear
items.comment:
Resets reusable storage owned by the allocator's concrete policy.

Parameters:
  self : ^Allocator - allocator whose reusable storage is reset.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - policy result pointer and operation status.

Notes:
  - Existing pointers may be overwritten by subsequent allocations.
items.summary: Resets reusable storage owned by the allocator's concrete policy.

items.name: free
items.comment:
Releases a raw pointer through the allocator's concrete policy.

Parameters:
  self : ^Allocator - allocator that owns the storage.
  ptr  : RawPtr     - pointer submitted for release.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - policy result pointer and operation status.

Notes:
  - Permanent and arena allocators do not reclaim individual allocations.
items.summary: Releases a raw pointer through the allocator's concrete policy.

items.name: destroy
items.comment:
Destroys the allocator's concrete policy and its owned backing storage.

Parameters:
  self : ^Allocator - allocator to destroy.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - policy result pointer and operation status.

Notes:
  - Outstanding heap allocations must be freed individually before destruction.
  - The allocator must not be used after this call.
items.summary: Destroys the allocator's concrete policy and its owned backing storage.

items.name: allocate
items.comment:
Allocates enough memory for one value of type T and returns the typed pointer.

Parameters:
  self : ^Allocator - allocator used to reserve the storage.

Returns:
  ^T - typed pointer to the allocated storage.

Notes:
  - The caller owns the returned storage.
  - Release it through the same allocator, for example with deallocate<T>.
items.summary: Allocates enough memory for one value of type T and returns the typed pointer.

items.name: deallocate
items.comment:
Frees a pointer previously allocated through the allocator, then clears the
caller's pointer slot to null.

Parameters:
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator that owns the storage.
  ptr       : ^^T        - address of the caller's typed pointer.
items.summary: Frees a pointer previously allocated through the allocator, then clears the caller's pointer slot to null.

items.name: InitArrayList
items.comment:
Constructs an ArrayList with the default capacity and context allocator.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  ArrayList<T> - initialized list with `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY`, the current
                 context allocator, and zero elements.

Notes:
  - This allocates backing storage for `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY` elements.
  - Allocation failure is reflected by `data` remaining null.
items.summary: Constructs an ArrayList with the default capacity and context allocator.

items.name: InitArrayList
items.comment:
Constructs an ArrayList with a requested capacity and allocator.

Parameters:
  capacity  : i64        - initial element capacity to allocate.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for the backing storage.

Returns:
  ArrayList<T> - initialized list with the requested capacity, allocator,
                 and zero elements.

Notes:
  - Allocation failure is reflected by `data` remaining null.
items.summary: Constructs an ArrayList with a requested capacity and allocator.

items.name: InitArrayList
items.comment:
Constructs an ArrayList with a requested capacity and context allocator.

Parameters:
  capacity : i64 - initial element capacity to allocate.

Returns:
  ArrayList<T> - initialized list with the requested capacity, the current
                 context allocator, and zero elements.

Notes:
  - Allocation failure is reflected by `data` remaining null.
items.summary: Constructs an ArrayList with a requested capacity and context allocator.

items.name: InitArrayList
items.comment:
Constructs an ArrayList with the default capacity and an allocator.

Parameters:
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator to associate with the list.

Returns:
  ArrayList<T> - initialized list with `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY`, the supplied
                 allocator, and zero elements.

Notes:
  - This allocates backing storage for `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY` elements.
  - Allocation failure is reflected by `data` remaining null.
items.summary: Constructs an ArrayList with the default capacity and an allocator.

items.name: DeinitArrayList
items.comment:
Frees an ArrayList's backing storage and resets its fields.

Parameters:
  list : ^ArrayList<T> - list to destroy. Must have a valid allocator.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - This frees only the list's internal buffer. It does not recursively
    destroy values stored in the list.
items.summary: Frees an ArrayList's backing storage and resets its fields.

items.name: as_slice
items.comment:
Creates a slice view over the live elements of an ArrayList.

Parameters:
  self : ^ArrayList<T> - list to view.

Returns:
  []T - slice view over `self.data` with length `self.count`.

Notes:
  - The returned slice does not own the backing storage.
  - Mutating or freeing the list may invalidate the slice.
items.summary: Creates a slice view over the live elements of an ArrayList.

items.name: get_at
items.comment:
Returns the element at an index.

Parameters:
  self  : ^ArrayList<T> - list to read from.
  index : i32           - zero-based element index.

Returns:
  [T, ContainerStatus] - element value and status.
                        On success returns the value and ContainerStatus.Ok.
                        On failure returns a default T value and:
                          ContainerStatus.IndexOutOfRange - `self` was null
                            or `index` was outside the live item range.
items.summary: Returns the element at an index.

items.name: add
items.comment:
Appends a value to the end of an ArrayList, growing the backing storage when
full.

Parameters:
  self  : ^ArrayList<T> - list to mutate. Must be initialized.
  value : T             - value to append.

Returns:
  bool - true when the value was appended, false if the list was invalid or
         allocation failed while growing.

Notes:
  - Growth doubles capacity, falling back to ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY when the
    current capacity is zero or negative.
items.summary: Appends a value to the end of an ArrayList, growing the backing storage when full.

items.name: increase_capacity
items.comment:
Reallocates an ArrayList backing buffer to the requested capacity.

Parameters:
  self     : ^ArrayList<T> - list to resize. Must have a valid allocator.
  capacity : i32           - requested element capacity. Must be at least
                             `self.count`.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - resize result and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           On failure returns false and:
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidAllocator - list or
                               allocator was invalid.
                             ContainerStatus.ArgOutOfRange - requested
                               capacity was smaller than live count.
                             ContainerStatus.AllocatorFailed - allocation
                               failed.

Notes:
  - Existing live elements are copied into the new buffer.
  - This does not initialize unused capacity.
items.summary: Reallocates an ArrayList backing buffer to the requested capacity.

items.name: remove_at
items.comment:
Removes the element at an index by swapping the final live element into its
slot.

Parameters:
  self  : ^ArrayList<T> - list to mutate.
  index : i32           - zero-based element index to remove.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - removal result and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           Returns ContainerStatus.InvalidContainer when
                           `self` is null.
                           Returns ContainerStatus.IndexOutOfRange when
                           `index` is outside the live item range.

Notes:
  - This does not preserve element order.
items.summary: Removes the element at an index by swapping the final live element into its slot.

items.name: remove
items.signature: remove : func<T>(self : ^ArrayList<T>, value : T, eq : func(T, T) -> bool ) -> [bool, ContainerStatus]
items.comment:
Removes the first element equal to `value` according to a caller-provided
equality function.

Parameters:
  self  : ^ArrayList<T>       - list to mutate.
  value : T                   - value to remove.
  eq    : func(T, T) -> bool  - equality predicate used to compare elements.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - removal result and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           If absent returns [false, ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound].

Notes:
  - This does not preserve element order because removal swaps with the last
    live element.
items.summary: Removes the first element equal to `value` according to a caller-provided equality function.

items.name: remove_range
items.signature: remove_range : func<T>(self : ^ArrayList<T>, index : i32, count : i32 ) -> [bool, ContainerStatus]
items.comment:
Removes a range of elements starting at `index`.

Parameters:
  self  : ^ArrayList<T> - list to mutate.
  index : i32           - first index to remove.
  count : i32           - number of elements to remove.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - range removal result and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           Returns ContainerStatus.IndexOutOfRange when the
                           requested range exceeds the live item range.

Notes:
  - This uses `remove_at`, so element order is not preserved.
items.summary: Removes a range of elements starting at `index`.

items.name: contains
items.comment:
Reports whether a list contains a value using the built-in `==` operator.

Parameters:
  self  : ^ArrayList<T> - list to search.
  value : T             - value to find.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - containment result and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           If absent returns [false, ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound].

Notes:
  - T must support the built-in `==` operator.
items.summary: Reports whether a list contains a value using the built-in `==` operator.

items.name: contains
items.signature: contains : func<T>(self : ^ArrayList<T>, value : T, eq : func(T, T) -> bool) -> [bool, ContainerStatus]
items.comment:
Reports whether a list contains a value using a caller-provided equality
function.

Parameters:
  self  : ^ArrayList<T>       - list to search.
  value : T                   - value to find.
  eq    : func(T, T) -> bool  - equality predicate used to compare elements.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - containment result and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           If absent returns [false, ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound].
items.summary: Reports whether a list contains a value using a caller-provided equality function.

items.name: clear
items.comment:
Removes all live elements from an ArrayList without freeing capacity.

Parameters:
  self : ^ArrayList<T> - list to clear. May be null, in which case this is a
                         no-op.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - This does not recursively destroy values stored in the list.
items.summary: Removes all live elements from an ArrayList without freeing capacity.

items.name: clone
items.comment:
Creates a shallow copy of an ArrayList and its live backing storage.

Parameters:
  self : ^ArrayList<T> - list to clone.

Returns:
  ArrayList<T> - new list with copied live elements and the same capacity.

Notes:
  - Values are copied byte-for-byte; pointed-to resources are not cloned.
  - The returned list uses the same allocator as `self`.
items.summary: Creates a shallow copy of an ArrayList and its live backing storage.

items.name: swap
items.signature: swap : func<T>(self: ^ArrayList<T>, idx0 : i32, idx1 : i32 ) -> bool
items.comment:
Swaps two live elements in an ArrayList.

Parameters:
  self : ^ArrayList<T> - list to mutate.
  idx0 : i32           - first element index.
  idx1 : i32           - second element index.

Returns:
  bool - true when both indexes were valid and the swap completed; false
         otherwise.
items.summary: Swaps two live elements in an ArrayList.

items.name: InitMap
items.comment:
Constructs a Map with the default capacity and context allocator.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  [Map<K,V>, ContainerStatus] - the initialized map header and status.
                               On success returns ContainerStatus.Ok.
                               A missing context allocator returns
                               ContainerStatus.InvalidAllocator.
                               Allocation failure returns
                               ContainerStatus.AllocatorFailed.

Notes:
  - The default capacity is `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY`.
  - This allocates the initial entry buffer.
items.summary: Constructs a Map with the default capacity and context allocator.

items.name: InitMap
items.comment:
Constructs a Map with a requested capacity and allocator.

Parameters:
  capacity  : i32        - requested initial slot capacity. Rounded up to
                           the next power of two when necessary.
  allocator : ^Allocator - non-null allocator to associate with the map.
Returns:
  [Map<K,V>, ContainerStatus] - the constructed map and a status.
                               On success returns ContainerStatus.Ok.
                               On failure returns a zero-valued map and:
                                 ContainerStatus.InvalidAllocator -
                                   `allocator` was null.
                                 ContainerStatus.InvalidArg -
                                   `capacity` was invalid.
                                 ContainerStatus.AllocatorFailed -
                                   backing storage allocation failed.

Notes:
  - K must provide `get_hash()` and `are_equals(other : K)` extension methods.
  - This allocates the initial entry buffer.
items.summary: Constructs a Map with a requested capacity and allocator.

items.name: InitMap
items.comment:
Constructs a Map with a requested capacity and context allocator.

Parameters:
  capacity : i32 - requested slot capacity. Rounded up to the next power
                   of two when necessary.

Returns:
  [Map<K,V>, ContainerStatus] - the initialized map header and status.
                               Returns ContainerStatus.InvalidArg when
                               `capacity` is not positive.
                               Returns ContainerStatus.InvalidAllocator
                               when the context allocator is null.
                               Returns ContainerStatus.AllocatorFailed
                               when backing storage allocation fails.

Notes:
  - This allocates the initial entry buffer.
items.summary: Constructs a Map with a requested capacity and context allocator.

items.name: InitMap
items.comment:
Constructs a Map with the default capacity and an allocator.

Parameters:

Returns:
  [Map<K,V>, ContainerStatus] - the initialized map header and status.
                               Returns ContainerStatus.InvalidAllocator
                               when `allocator` is null.
                               Returns ContainerStatus.AllocatorFailed
                               when backing storage allocation fails.

Notes:
  - The default capacity is `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY`.
  - This allocates the initial entry buffer.

items.name: DeinitMap
items.comment:
Releases the backing storage owned by a Map and resets its fields.

Parameters:
  map : ^Map<K,V> - map to deinitialize. May be null.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - This frees only the map's internal entry buffer. It does not recursively
    destroy keys or values stored inside entries.
items.summary: Releases the backing storage owned by a Map and resets its fields.

items.name: add
items.signature: add : func<K,V>(self : ^Map<K,V>, key : K, value : V) -> [bool, ContainerStatus]
items.comment:
Inserts a key/value pair into a Map, or updates the value for an existing key.

Parameters:
  self  : ^Map<K,V> - map to mutate. Must be initialized.
  key   : K         - key to insert or update.
  value : V         - value to store for the key.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - insertion flag and status.
                           On success:
                             [true,  ContainerStatus.Ok] - inserted new key.
                             [false, ContainerStatus.Ok] - updated existing key.
                           On failure:
                             ContainerStatus.InternalError      - `self` was null.
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidContainer  - backing storage
                               was invalid or no slot could be found.
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidArg         - capacity was invalid.
                             Any ContainerStatus propagated from reserve.

Notes:
  - The map grows before insertion when live entries plus tombstones reach
    the configured load threshold.
  - Deleted slots marked as tombstones may be reused for new entries.
items.summary: Inserts a key/value pair into a Map, or updates the value for an existing key.

items.name: get
items.comment:
Looks up a value by key.

Parameters:
  self : ^Map<K,V> - map to search. Must be initialized.
  key  : K         - key to find.

Returns:
  [V, ContainerStatus] - found value and status.
                        On success returns the stored value and
                        ContainerStatus.Ok.
                        On failure returns a default V value and:
                          ContainerStatus.InternalError     - `self` was null.
                          ContainerStatus.InvalidContainer - backing storage
                            was invalid.
                          ContainerStatus.InvalidArg        - capacity was invalid.
                          ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound      - key was absent.
items.summary: Looks up a value by key.

items.name: contains
items.comment:
Reports whether a Map contains a key.

Parameters:
  self : ^Map<K,V> - map to search. Must be initialized.
  key  : K         - key to find.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - containment result and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           If absent returns [false, ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound].
                           On invalid input returns false with:
                             ContainerStatus.InternalError
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidContainer
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidArg
items.summary: Reports whether a Map contains a key.

items.name: remove
items.comment:
Removes a key/value pair from a Map.

Parameters:
  self : ^Map<K,V> - map to mutate. Must be initialized.
  key  : K         - key to remove.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - removal flag and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           If absent returns [false, ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound].
                           On invalid input returns false with:
                             ContainerStatus.InternalError
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidContainer
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidArg

Notes:
  - Removed slots become tombstones so existing probe chains remain valid.
  - This does not recursively destroy the removed key or value.
items.summary: Removes a key/value pair from a Map.

items.name: clear
items.comment:
Removes all entries from a Map while keeping its allocated capacity.

Parameters:
  self : ^Map<K,V> - map to clear. Must be initialized.

Returns:
  ContainerStatus - ContainerStatus.Ok on success, or:
                     ContainerStatus.InternalError     - `self` was null.
                     ContainerStatus.InvalidContainer - backing storage was invalid.
                     ContainerStatus.InvalidArg        - capacity was invalid.

Notes:
  - All slots are reset to Empty and the tombstone count is reset to zero.
  - This does not recursively destroy keys or values stored inside entries.
items.summary: Removes all entries from a Map while keeping its allocated capacity.
