  capacity  : i32        - requested initial capacity. Rounded up to the
                           next power of two when necessary.
  allocator : ^Allocator - non-null allocator used for backing storage.

Returns:
  [Set<T>, ContainerStatus] - initialized set and status.
                             On success returns ContainerStatus.Ok.
                             A null allocator returns
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidAllocator.
                             Invalid capacity returns
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidArg.
                             Allocation failure returns
                             ContainerStatus.AllocatorFailed.

Notes:
  - T must provide `get_hash()` and `are_equals(other : T)` extension methods.
  - This allocates the initial Map entry buffer.
items.summary: Constructs a Set with a requested capacity and allocator.

items.name: DeinitSet
items.comment:
Releases the backing storage owned by a Set and resets its internal Map.

Parameters:
  set : ^Set<T> - set to deinitialize. May be null.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - This frees only the internal Map entry buffer owned by the Set.
  - It does not recursively destroy values stored in the Set.
  - It does not free the Set value or pointer itself.
items.summary: Releases the backing storage owned by a Set and resets its internal Map.

items.name: add
items.comment:
Adds a value to a Set.

Parameters:
  self  : ^Set<T> - set to mutate. Must be initialized.
  value : T       - value to add.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - insertion flag and status.
                           On success:
                             [true,  ContainerStatus.Ok] - value was new.
                             [false, ContainerStatus.Ok] - value already existed.
                           Other statuses are propagated from Map.add.

Notes:
  - T must provide `get_hash()` and `are_equals(other : T)` extension methods.
items.summary: Adds a value to a Set.

items.name: contains
items.comment:
Reports whether a Set contains a value.

Parameters:
  self  : ^Set<T> - set to search. Must be initialized.
  value : T       - value to find.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - containment result and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           If absent returns
                           [false, ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound].
                           Other statuses are propagated from Map.contains.

Notes:
  - T must provide `get_hash()` and `are_equals(other : T)` extension methods.
items.summary: Reports whether a Set contains a value.

items.name: remove
items.comment:
Removes a value from a Set.

Parameters:
  self  : ^Set<T> - set to mutate. Must be initialized.
  value : T       - value to remove.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - removal flag and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           If absent returns
                           [false, ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound].
                           Other statuses are propagated from Map.remove.

Notes:
  - This does not recursively destroy the removed value.
items.summary: Removes a value from a Set.

items.name: clear
items.comment:
Removes all values from a Set while keeping its allocated capacity.

Parameters:
  self : ^Set<T> - set to clear. Must be initialized.

Returns:
  ContainerStatus - ContainerStatus.Ok on success. Other statuses are
                    propagated from Map.clear.

Notes:
  - This does not recursively destroy values stored in the Set.
items.summary: Removes all values from a Set while keeping its allocated capacity.

items.name: count
items.comment:
Returns the number of values in a Set.

Parameters:
  self : ^Set<T> - set to query.

Returns:
  i64 - live value count, or zero for a null Set.
items.summary: Returns the number of values in a Set.

items.name: empty
items.comment:
Reports whether a Set contains no values.

Parameters:
  self : ^Set<T> - set to query.

Returns:
  bool - true when the Set is null or contains no values.
items.summary: Reports whether a Set contains no values.

items.name: Stack
items.comment: Last-in, first-out container backed by ArrayList<T>.
items.summary: Last-in, first-out container backed by ArrayList<T>.

items.name: InitStack
items.comment:
Constructs a Stack with the default capacity and context allocator.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  Stack<T> - stack with `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY`, the current context
             allocator, and zero elements.

Notes:
  - This allocates backing storage for `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY` elements.
  - Allocation failure is reflected by `items.data` remaining null.
items.summary: Constructs a Stack with the default capacity and context allocator.

items.name: InitStack
items.comment:
Constructs a Stack with a requested capacity and allocator.

Parameters:
  capacity  : i64        - initial element capacity to allocate.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for the backing storage.

Returns:
  Stack<T> - stack with the requested capacity and allocator, and zero
             elements.

Notes:
  - Allocation failure is reflected by `items.data` remaining null.
items.summary: Constructs a Stack with a requested capacity and allocator.

items.name: InitStack
items.comment:
Constructs a Stack with a requested capacity and context allocator.

Parameters:
  capacity : i64 - initial element capacity to allocate.

Returns:
  Stack<T> - stack with the requested capacity, the current context
             allocator, and zero elements.

Notes:
  - Allocation failure is reflected by `items.data` remaining null.
items.summary: Constructs a Stack with a requested capacity and context allocator.

items.name: InitStack
items.comment:
Constructs a Stack with the default capacity and an allocator.

Parameters:
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator to associate with the stack.

Returns:
  Stack<T> - stack with `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY`, the supplied allocator,
             and zero elements.

Notes:
  - This allocates backing storage for `ARRAY_DEFAULT_CAPACITY` elements.
  - Allocation failure is reflected by `items.data` remaining null.
items.summary: Constructs a Stack with the default capacity and an allocator.

items.name: DeinitStack
items.comment:
Frees a Stack's backing storage and resets its internal list.

Parameters:
  stack : ^Stack<T> - stack to deinitialize. May be null.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - This frees only the internal buffer. It does not recursively destroy
    values stored in the stack.
items.summary: Frees a Stack's backing storage and resets its internal list.

items.name: push
items.comment:
Pushes a value onto the top of the stack.

Parameters:
  self  : ^Stack<T> - stack to mutate.
  value : T         - value to push.

Returns:
  [bool, ContainerStatus] - push result and status.
                           On success returns [true, ContainerStatus.Ok].
                           On failure returns false with:
                             ContainerStatus.InvalidContainer
                             ContainerStatus.AllocatorFailed
items.summary: Pushes a value onto the top of the stack.

items.name: pop
items.comment:
Removes and returns the top value from the stack.

Parameters:
  self : ^Stack<T> - stack to mutate.

Returns:
  [T, ContainerStatus] - popped value and status.
                        On empty or invalid stack, returns a default T value
                        with ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound or
                        ContainerStatus.InvalidContainer.
items.summary: Removes and returns the top value from the stack.

items.name: peek
items.comment:
Returns the top value without removing it.

Parameters:
  self : ^Stack<T> - stack to read from.

Returns:
  [T, ContainerStatus] - top value and status.
                        On empty or invalid stack, returns a default T value
                        with ContainerStatus.ItemNotFound or
                        ContainerStatus.InvalidContainer.
items.summary: Returns the top value without removing it.

items.name: clear
items.comment:
Removes all values from a stack without freeing capacity.

Parameters:
  self : ^Stack<T> - stack to clear. May be null.

Returns:
  void
items.summary: Removes all values from a stack without freeing capacity.

items.name: empty
items.comment:
Reports whether a stack contains no values.

Parameters:
  self : ^Stack<T> - stack to query.

Returns:
  bool - true when the stack is null or contains no values.
items.summary: Reports whether a stack contains no values.

items.name: count
items.comment:
Returns the number of live values in a stack.

Parameters:
  self : ^Stack<T> - stack to query.

Returns:
  i64 - live value count, or zero for a null stack.
items.summary: Returns the number of live values in a stack.

items.name: print
items.comment:
Formats `fmt` with the provided arguments and writes the result to stdout
without appending a trailing newline, using a caller-provided allocator.

Parameters:
  allocator : ^Allocator  - allocator used for the temporary formatted
                            string. Must be non-null.
  fmt       : string      - format string containing formatter markers such as
                            `{v}`, `{d}`, `{b}`, `{f}`, `{s}`, or `{c}`.
  args      : ...any      - values consumed by formatter markers in
                            left-to-right order.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - The temporary string is freed before this function returns.
  - The allocator itself is not destroyed by this overload.
items.summary: Formats `fmt` with the provided arguments and writes the result to stdout without appending a trailing newline, using a caller-provided allocator.

items.name: print
items.comment:
Formats `fmt` with the provided arguments and writes the result to stdout
without appending a trailing newline.

Parameters:
  fmt  : string  - format string containing formatter markers such as
                   `{v}`, `{d}`, `{b}`, `{f}`, `{s}`, or `{c}`.
  args : ...any  - values consumed by formatter markers in left-to-right
                   order.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - Uses a temporary heap allocator for the formatted string.
  - Formatter arguments are type-erased as `any` and resolved at runtime.
items.summary: Formats `fmt` with the provided arguments and writes the result to stdout without appending a trailing newline.

items.name: println
items.comment:
Formats `fmt` with the provided arguments and writes the result to stdout
followed by a newline, using a caller-provided allocator.

Parameters:
  allocator : ^Allocator  - allocator used for the temporary formatted
                            string. Must be non-null.
  fmt       : string      - format string containing formatter markers such as
                            `{v}`, `{d}`, `{b}`, `{f}`, `{s}`, or `{c}`.
  args      : ...any      - values consumed by formatter markers in
                            left-to-right order.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - The temporary string is freed before this function returns.
  - The allocator itself is not destroyed by this overload.
items.summary: Formats `fmt` with the provided arguments and writes the result to stdout followed by a newline, using a caller-provided allocator.

items.name: println
items.comment:
Formats `fmt` with the provided arguments and writes the result to stdout
followed by a newline.

Parameters:
  fmt  : string  - format string containing formatter markers such as
                   `{v}`, `{d}`, `{b}`, `{f}`, `{s}`, or `{c}`.
  args : ...any  - values consumed by formatter markers in left-to-right
                   order.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - Uses a temporary heap allocator for the formatted string.
  - Prefer `print` when the caller wants to control line endings.
items.summary: Formats `fmt` with the provided arguments and writes the result to stdout followed by a newline.

items.name: println
items.comment:
Writes a newline to stdout.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - Does not create a temporary formatted string or allocator.
items.summary: Writes a newline to stdout.

items.name: format_string
items.signature: format_string : func(allocator : ^Allocator, fmt : string, args : ...any) -> string
items.comment:
Builds an owned string by replacing formatter markers in `fmt` with the
corresponding values from `args`.

Parameters:
  allocator : ^Allocator  - allocator used to allocate the returned string.
                            Must be non-null.
  fmt       : string      - format string containing formatter markers such as
                            `{v}`, `{d}`, `{b}`, `{f}`, `{s}`, or `{c}`.
  args      : ...any      - values consumed by formatter markers in left-to-right
                            order.

Returns:
  string - formatted string allocated with `allocator`, or an empty string
           when `allocator` is null or `fmt` is empty.

Notes:
  - The caller owns the returned string and must release it with
    `free_string` using the same allocator.
  - `{v}` uses the default representation for the argument's runtime type.
items.summary: Builds an owned string by replacing formatter markers in `fmt` with the corresponding values from `args`.

items.name: CachedGlyph
items.comment:
A value copy of cached glyph data. Atlas coordinates and UVs remain stable
for the lifetime of the FontSystem because a full atlas never repacks.
items.summary: A value copy of cached glyph data. Atlas coordinates and UVs remain stable for the lifetime of the FontSystem because a full atlas never repacks.

items.name: FontAtlas
items.comment:
CPU-owned 8-bit grayscale atlas. Pixels are allocated lazily on the first
non-empty cached glyph. A renderer may upload pixels when dirty is true and
call font_system_mark_atlas_clean after observing revision.
items.summary: CPU-owned 8-bit grayscale atlas. Pixels are allocated lazily on the first non-empty cached glyph. A renderer may upload pixels when dirty is true and call font_system_mark_atlas_clean after observing revision.

items.name: font_system_get_cached_glyph
items.signature: font_system_get_cached_glyph : func( self : ^FontSystem, font_id : FontId, codepoint : rune) -> [CachedGlyph, FontStatus]
items.comment:
Returns a stable value copy. A cache hit performs no allocation,
rasterization, atlas packing, or revision change.
items.summary: Returns a stable value copy. A cache hit performs no allocation, rasterization, atlas packing, or revision change.

items.name: font_system_mark_atlas_clean
items.comment:
Marks the current atlas revision as observed by a renderer. Adding another
non-empty glyph will set dirty again and increment revision.
items.summary: Marks the current atlas revision as observed by a renderer. Adding another non-empty glyph will set dirty again and increment revision.

items.name: Font
items.comment:
A Font is either a sized face instance or an immutable ordered fallback
chain. Chains copy the primary member's layout metrics and own no face data.
items.summary: A Font is either a sized face instance or an immutable ordered fallback chain. Chains copy the primary member's layout metrics and own no face data.

items.name: ResolvedGlyph
items.comment:
Resolution identifies the sized font that owns glyph_index. Pair kerning,
glyph caching, and rasterization must use font_id rather than a logical
fallback-chain ID.
items.summary: Resolution identifies the sized font that owns glyph_index. Pair kerning, glyph caching, and rasterization must use font_id rather than a logical fallback-chain ID.

items.name: GlyphBitmap
items.comment:
Owns pixels allocated by FontSystem's allocator. DestroyGlyphBitmap must be
called before that allocator is destroyed. When FontSystem owns the
allocator, release the bitmap before DestroyFontSystem.
items.summary: Owns pixels allocated by FontSystem's allocator. DestroyGlyphBitmap must be called before that allocator is destroyed. When FontSystem owns the allocator, release the bitmap before DestroyFontSystem.

items.name: add_font_folder
items.comment:
Font folders are searched in insertion order after load_ttf_font fails to
open the path as supplied. Folder strings are copied into FontSystem-owned
storage and remain valid until DestroyFontSystem.
items.summary: Font folders are searched in insertion order after load_ttf_font fails to open the path as supplied. Folder strings are copied into FontSystem-owned storage and remain valid until DestroyFontSystem.

items.name: load_ttf_font
items.comment:
Loads a trusted TrueType/OpenType font by path. If the path cannot be
opened directly, each registered font folder is searched in order.
items.summary: Loads a trusted TrueType/OpenType font by path. If the path cannot be opened directly, each registered font folder is searched in order.

items.name: font_system_get_face
items.comment:
Returned pointers are borrowed views and may be invalidated when another face
is added. Persist FaceId rather than the pointer.
items.summary: Returned pointers are borrowed views and may be invalidated when another face is added. Persist FaceId rather than the pointer.

items.name: font_system_get_font
items.comment:
Returned pointers are borrowed views and may be invalidated when another
sized instance is added. Persist FontId rather than the pointer.
items.summary: Returned pointers are borrowed views and may be invalidated when another sized instance is added. Persist FontId rather than the pointer.

items.name: font_system_load_face_memory
items.signature: font_system_load_face_memory : func( self : ^FontSystem, data : []u8, metrics : FontFaceMetrics, ownership : FontMemoryOwnership) -> [FaceId, FontStatus]
items.comment:
Registers encoded font bytes and their design-unit metrics. Borrowed bytes
must outlive the face; Copied bytes become FontSystem-owned.
items.summary: Registers encoded font bytes and their design-unit metrics. Borrowed bytes must outlive the face; Copied bytes become FontSystem-owned.

items.name: font_system_load_truetype_memory
items.signature: font_system_load_truetype_memory : func( self : ^FontSystem, data : []u8, ownership : FontMemoryOwnership) -> [FaceId, FontStatus]
items.comment:
Parses the first TrueType/OpenType face in trusted data through stb_truetype.
Face metrics are read from the font; callers do not supply design-unit metrics.
Borrowed bytes must outlive the face. Copied bytes are released by
DestroyFontSystem. stb_truetype is not a hardened parser for hostile input.
items.summary: Parses the first TrueType/OpenType face in trusted data through stb_truetype. Face metrics are read from the font; callers do not supply design-unit metrics. Borrowed bytes must outlive the face. Copied bytes are released by DestroyFontSystem. stb_truetype is not a hardened parser for hostile input.

items.name: font_system_load_truetype_file
items.signature: font_system_load_truetype_file : func( self : ^FontSystem, path : string) -> [FaceId, FontStatus]
items.comment:
Loads and owns the first trusted TrueType/OpenType face in path. The file
buffer is retained because stb_truetype face data must stay alive until
destruction. Do not use this parser for untrusted font files.
items.summary: Loads and owns the first trusted TrueType/OpenType face in path. The file buffer is retained because stb_truetype face data must stay alive until destruction. Do not use this parser for untrusted font files.

items.name: font_system_create_font
items.signature: font_system_create_font : func( self : ^FontSystem, face_id : FaceId, size : f32, line_height : f32) -> [FontId, FontStatus]
items.comment:
Creates or reuses a sized face instance. A non-positive line_height selects
the natural line height derived from the face metrics.
items.summary: Creates or reuses a sized face instance. A non-positive line_height selects the natural line height derived from the face metrics.

items.name: font_system_create_font_chain
items.comment:
Creates an immutable logical font from ordered sized TrueType fonts. The
first member owns line metrics and baseline placement. Chain members cannot
themselves be chains, which keeps resolution deterministic and cycle-free.
items.summary: Creates an immutable logical font from ordered sized TrueType fonts. The first member owns line metrics and baseline placement. Chain members cannot themselves be chains, which keeps resolution deterministic and cycle-free.

items.name: font_system_resolve_glyph
items.signature: font_system_resolve_glyph : func( self : ^FontSystem, font_id : FontId, codepoint : rune) -> [ResolvedGlyph, FontStatus]
items.comment:
Resolves one Unicode scalar to the first sized font that contains it. If no
chain member contains the scalar, the primary font's glyph-zero metrics are
returned so missing-glyph behavior stays deterministic.
items.summary: Resolves one Unicode scalar to the first sized font that contains it. If no chain member contains the scalar, the primary font's glyph-zero metrics are returned so missing-glyph behavior stays deterministic.

items.name: font_system_get_glyph_metrics
items.signature: font_system_get_glyph_metrics : func( self : ^FontSystem, font_id : FontId, codepoint : rune) -> [GlyphMetrics, FontStatus]
items.comment:
Resolves a Unicode scalar through a sized or logical fallback font. Call
font_system_resolve_glyph when the actual FontId is also required.
items.summary: Resolves a Unicode scalar through a sized or logical fallback font. Call font_system_resolve_glyph when the actual FontId is also required.

items.name: font_system_get_glyph_kerning
items.signature: font_system_get_glyph_kerning : func( self : ^FontSystem, font_id : FontId, left_glyph_index : i32, right_glyph_index : i32) -> [f32, FontStatus]
items.comment:
Returns the scaled horizontal adjustment between two resolved glyphs in a
sized TrueType font. Glyph zero represents a missing Unicode scalar and
deliberately contributes no kerning. This query does not allocate.
items.summary: Returns the scaled horizontal adjustment between two resolved glyphs in a sized TrueType font. Glyph zero represents a missing Unicode scalar and deliberately contributes no kerning. This query does not allocate.

items.name: font_system_rasterize_glyph
items.signature: font_system_rasterize_glyph : func( self : ^FontSystem, font_id : FontId, codepoint : rune) -> [GlyphBitmap, FontStatus]
items.comment:
Allocates and rasterizes an 8-bit grayscale glyph bitmap. Empty glyphs such
as spaces return Ok with no allocation. The caller owns the returned pixels
and releases them with DestroyGlyphBitmap.
items.summary: Allocates and rasterizes an 8-bit grayscale glyph bitmap. Empty glyphs such as spaces return Ok with no allocation. The caller owns the returned pixels and releases them with DestroyGlyphBitmap.

items.name: FontSystemWithAtlasSize
items.signature: FontSystemWithAtlasSize : func( allocator : ^Allocator, owns_allocator : bool, atlas_width : i32, atlas_height : i32) -> ^FontSystem
items.comment:
Creates a FontSystem. owns_allocator controls whether DestroyFontSystem also
destroys and releases the allocator object supplied here.
items.summary: Creates a FontSystem. owns_allocator controls whether DestroyFontSystem also destroys and releases the allocator object supplied here.

items.name: FontSystem
items.comment:
Creates a FontSystem with a stable library-owned default atlas size. Atlas
pixels remain unallocated until the first non-empty cached glyph.
items.summary: Creates a FontSystem with a stable library-owned default atlas size. Atlas pixels remain unallocated until the first non-empty cached glyph.

items.name: DestroyFontSystem
items.comment:
Releases copied face bytes and all sized instances. When owns_allocator was
true at construction, this also destroys and releases the allocator object.
items.summary: Releases copied face bytes and all sized instances. When owns_allocator was true at construction, this also destroys and releases the allocator object.

items.name: Screen
items.comment: UI area dimensions in whole logical units, using the mouse input coordinate space.
items.summary: UI area dimensions in whole logical units, using the mouse input coordinate space.

items.name: FileDesc
items.comment:
Owns an open file descriptor and records the mode and borrowed path used to
open it. Call close(^FileDesc) exactly once to close the handle and release
the descriptor.
items.summary: Owns an open file descriptor and records the mode and borrowed path used to open it. Call close(^FileDesc) exactly once to close the handle and release the descriptor.

items.name: open
items.signature: open : func(path : string, options : FileMode) -> [^FileDesc, IoStatus]
items.comment:
Opens a file using the requested mode.

Parameters:
  path    : string       - borrowed filesystem path.
  options : FileMode - requested access and creation mode.

Returns:
  [^FileDesc, IoStatus] - owned descriptor and operation status. The
                          descriptor is null on failure.

Notes:
  - The returned descriptor owns its OS handle.
  - The path header is borrowed; its backing storage must remain valid while
    the descriptor is in use.
  - Call close(^FileDesc) exactly once to close and release the descriptor.
items.summary: Opens a file using the requested mode.

items.name: open_read
items.comment:
Opens an existing file for reading.

Parameters:
  path : string - borrowed filesystem path.

Returns:
  [^FileDesc, IoStatus] - owned descriptor and operation status.
items.summary: Opens an existing file for reading.

items.name: open_write
items.comment:
Creates or truncates a file and opens it for writing.

Parameters:
  path : string - borrowed filesystem path.

Returns:
  [^FileDesc, IoStatus] - owned descriptor and operation status.
items.summary: Creates or truncates a file and opens it for writing.

items.name: seek
items.signature: seek : func(file : ^FileDesc, offset : i64, origin : SeekOrigin) -> [i64, IoStatus]
items.comment:
Moves the position of an open file descriptor.

Parameters:
  file   : ^FileDesc - descriptor to reposition.
  offset : i64       - signed byte offset relative to origin.
  origin : SeekOrigin - reference position used to interpret offset.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - new absolute position with IoStatus.Ok on success, or
                    -1 with an error status on failure.
items.summary: Moves the position of an open file descriptor.

items.name: close
items.comment:
Closes and releases an owned file descriptor.

Parameters:
  file : ^FileDesc - descriptor returned by open, open_read, or open_write.

Returns:
  [bool, IoStatus] - true with IoStatus.Ok on success; false with an error
                     status when the descriptor or handle is invalid or the
                     OS close operation fails.

Notes:
  - The descriptor pointer is invalid after this call, even when the OS
    close operation reports an error.
items.summary: Closes and releases an owned file descriptor.

items.name: file_length
items.comment:
Returns the size in bytes of the file at `path` through the portable
OS metadata API.

Parameters:
  path : string - filesystem path to the file to query.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus]
    - On success: [<file size in bytes>, IoStatus.Ok]
    - On failure: [-1, IoStatus.InvalidFile] when metadata lookup fails
      (e.g. file missing, permission denied, broken path).

Notes:
  - Does not open or read the file; only its metadata is inspected.
items.summary: Returns the size in bytes of the file at `path` through the portable OS metadata API.

items.name: length
items.comment:
Returns the size in bytes of the file backing a FileDesc.

Parameters:
  file : ^FileDesc - descriptor whose underlying file size is queried.

Returns:
  i64 - size of the file in bytes, or -1 when metadata lookup fails.
items.summary: Returns the size in bytes of the file backing a FileDesc.

items.name: position
items.comment:
Returns the current byte offset of a FileDesc within its underlying
file.

Parameters:
  file : ^FileDesc - descriptor whose current position is queried.
                     Must be non-null and seekable.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - current byte offset and an error status.
                   On success returns the current position and IoStatus.Ok.
                   On failure returns -1 and:
                     IoStatus.InvalidFile      - `file` was null.
                     IoStatus.DontSupportSeek  - file is not seekable.
                     IoStatus.CannotSeek       - underlying OS seek failed.

Notes:
  - This queries the underlying OS file handle using SEEK_CUR without
    moving the cursor.
items.summary: Returns the current byte offset of a FileDesc within its underlying file.

items.name: opened
items.comment:
Reports whether a FileDesc's underlying handle is currently valid
and open.

Parameters:
  file : ^FileDesc - descriptor to query. Must be non-null.

Returns:
  [bool, IoStatus] - the open state of the file and an error status.
                    On success returns the validity of the handle and
                    the IoStatus reported by the platform check.
                    On failure returns:
                      IoStatus.InvalidFile - `file` was null.
items.summary: Reports whether a FileDesc's underlying handle is currently valid and open.

items.name: read_all_text
items.comment:
Reads the entire contents of the file at `path` into a single
`string`, allocated through the caller-supplied allocator.

Parameters:
  path      : string      - filesystem path to the file to read.
  allocator : ^Allocator  - allocator used to back the returned
                            string's buffer. Must be non-null.

Returns:
  [string, IoStatus]
    - On success: [<file contents>, IoStatus.Ok]
    - On failure: [string{}, IoStatus.InvalidFile] when the file
      does not exist or its size cannot be determined.
    - On failure: [string{}, IoStatus.InvalidAllocator] when
      `allocator` is null.
    - Other IoStatus values may propagate from opening or reading the file.

Notes:
  - Opens and closes a FileDesc internally.
  - The returned string is owned by the caller and must be released with
    the supplied allocator.
items.summary: Reads the entire contents of the file at `path` into a single `string`, allocated through the caller-supplied allocator.

items.name: read_all_text
items.comment:
Reads the entire contents of a FileDesc into a newly allocated
string.

Parameters:
  file : ^FileDesc - descriptor to read from. Must be non-null and readable.

Returns:
  [string, IoStatus] - the file contents and an error status.
                      On success returns the full file contents and
                      IoStatus.Ok.
                      On failure returns an empty string and:
                        IoStatus.InvalidFile      - `file` was null.
                        IoStatus.InvalidAllocator - context.allocator was null.
                        IoStatus.CannotRead       - file is not readable.
                        IoStatus.ReadError        - underlying read failed.

Notes:
  - The returned string is allocated with context.allocator; the caller is
    responsible for releasing it with that allocator.
items.summary: Reads the entire contents of a FileDesc into a newly allocated string.

items.name: read
items.signature: read : func(file : ^FileDesc, size : i64, buffer : ^[]i8) -> [i64, IoStatus]
items.comment:
Reads up to `size` bytes from a FileDesc into the caller's signed-byte
buffer.

Parameters:
  file   : ^FileDesc - descriptor to read from. Must be non-null and readable.
  size   : i64       - maximum number of bytes to read. Must fit in buffer.
  buffer : ^[]i8     - destination byte slice.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - number of bytes read and operation status.
                   On failure returns -1 and:
                     IoStatus.InvalidFile - `file` was null.
                     IoStatus.InvalidArg  - `buffer` was null, `size` or the
                                            buffer length was negative,
                                            `size` exceeded the buffer length,
                                            or a positive read had null data.
                     IoStatus.CannotRead  - file mode is not readable.
                     IoStatus.ReadError   - underlying OS read failed.
                   A zero size returns [0, IoStatus.Ok].
items.summary: Reads up to `size` bytes from a FileDesc into the caller's signed-byte buffer.

items.name: read_bytes
items.comment:
Reads up to `buffer.length` bytes from a FileDesc into the caller's
byte buffer.

Parameters:
  file   : ^FileDesc - descriptor to read from. Must be non-null and readable.
  buffer : ^[]u8     - destination byte slice; the slice's `length`
                       dictates how many bytes are requested.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - number of bytes read and an error status.
                   On success returns the byte count and IoStatus.Ok.
                   On failure returns -1 and:
                     IoStatus.InvalidFile      - `file` was null.
                     IoStatus.InvalidArg       - `buffer` was null, its
                                                 length was negative, or a
                                                 positive-length slice had
                                                 null data.
                     IoStatus.CannotRead       - file is not readable.
                     IoStatus.ReadError        - underlying OS read failed.
                   A zero-length buffer returns [0, IoStatus.Ok].
items.summary: Reads up to `buffer.length` bytes from a FileDesc into the caller's byte buffer.

items.name: read_line
items.comment:
Reads a single line of text from a FileDesc into a newly allocated
string.

Parameters:
  file : ^FileDesc - descriptor to read from. Must be non-null and readable.

Returns:
  [string, IoStatus] - line contents and an error status.
                      On success returns the line without the trailing
                      newline character and IoStatus.Ok.
                      On failure returns an empty string and:
                        IoStatus.InvalidFile      - `file` was null.
                        IoStatus.InvalidAllocator - context.allocator was null.
                        IoStatus.CannotRead       - file is not readable.
                        IoStatus.AllocatorFailed  - line buffer allocation failed.
                        IoStatus.ReadError        - underlying read failed.

Notes:
  - The returned string is allocated with context.allocator; the caller is
    responsible for releasing it with that allocator.
  - The returned string does not include the '\n' line terminator.
  - EOF before any bytes returns an empty string with IoStatus.Ok.
  - EOF after partial data returns that partial line with IoStatus.Ok.
items.summary: Reads a single line of text from a FileDesc into a newly allocated string.

items.name: write_bytes
items.comment:
Writes the complete contents of `buffer` to a FileDesc.

Parameters:
  file   : ^FileDesc - descriptor to write to. Must be non-null and writable.
  buffer : []u8     - source byte slice to write.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - number of bytes written and operation status.
                   On failure, the byte count reports any successfully
                   written prefix.
                   Validation failures return -1 and:
                     IoStatus.InvalidFile      - `file` was null.
                     IoStatus.InvalidArg       - `buffer.length` was negative
                                                 or positive with null data.
                     IoStatus.CannotWrite      - file mode is not writable.
                     IoStatus.WriteError       - an OS write failed.
items.summary: Writes the complete contents of `buffer` to a FileDesc.

items.name: write_string
items.comment:
Writes the contents of `str` to a FileDesc.

Parameters:
  file : ^FileDesc - descriptor to write to. Must be non-null and writable.
  str  : string    - source string whose bytes are written to the file.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - number of bytes written and operation status.
                   On failure returns the error propagated from
                   write_bytes.

Notes:
  - This is a convenience wrapper around write_bytes(str.to_slice()).
items.summary: Writes the contents of `str` to a FileDesc.

items.name: write
items.comment:
Writes the native in-memory byte representation of an i8 value.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - 1 and IoStatus.Ok on success, or the result propagated
                    from write_bytes on failure.
items.summary: Writes the native in-memory byte representation of an i8 value.

items.name: write
items.comment:
Writes the native-endian, in-memory byte representation of an i16 value.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - 2 and IoStatus.Ok on success, or the result propagated
                    from write_bytes on failure.
items.summary: Writes the native-endian, in-memory byte representation of an i16 value.

items.name: write
items.comment:
Writes the native-endian, in-memory byte representation of an i32 value.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - 4 and IoStatus.Ok on success, or the result propagated
                    from write_bytes on failure.
items.summary: Writes the native-endian, in-memory byte representation of an i32 value.

items.name: write
items.comment:
Writes the native-endian, in-memory byte representation of an i64 value.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - 8 and IoStatus.Ok on success, or the result propagated
                    from write_bytes on failure.
items.summary: Writes the native-endian, in-memory byte representation of an i64 value.

items.name: write
items.comment:
Writes the native in-memory byte representation of a bool value.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - sizeof(bool) and IoStatus.Ok on success, or the result
                    propagated from write_bytes on failure.
items.summary: Writes the native in-memory byte representation of a bool value.

items.name: write_all_bytes
items.comment:
Creates or truncates the file at `path` and writes all bytes from `data`.

Parameters:
  path : string - borrowed destination path.
  data : []byte - borrowed byte slice to write.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - bytes written and operation status. An open failure
                    returns -1. A write failure reports any completed prefix.
items.summary: Creates or truncates the file at `path` and writes all bytes from `data`.

items.name: write_all_text
items.signature: write_all_text : func(path : string, data : string) -> [i64, IoStatus]
items.comment:
Creates or truncates the file at `path` and writes all bytes from `data`.

Parameters:
  path : string - borrowed destination path.
  data : string - borrowed text to write without an added terminator.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - bytes written and operation status.
items.summary: Creates or truncates the file at `path` and writes all bytes from `data`.

items.name: write_lines
items.comment:
Creates or truncates the file at `path` and writes each string followed by
a newline byte.

Parameters:
  path  : string   - borrowed destination path.
  lines : []string - borrowed lines to write in order.

Returns:
  [i64, IoStatus] - total bytes written and operation status. The count
                    includes newline bytes and any prefix completed before
                    a write failure.

Notes:
  - Every input element receives a trailing '\n', including the last one.
  - An empty slice creates an empty file.
items.summary: Creates or truncates the file at `path` and writes each string followed by a newline byte.

items.name: DirEntry
items.comment:
Describes one entry returned by list_dir.

The name and path strings in a successful list_dir result are owned by the
result's allocator. The classification flags describe the entry itself and
never follow a link target.
items.summary: Describes one entry returned by list_dir.

items.name: DeinitDirEntries
items.comment:
Releases a directory listing and all storage owned by it.

Parameters:
  entries : ^containers.ArrayList<DirEntry> - list returned by list_dir.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - Frees every entry name, every entry path, and the ArrayList backing
    buffer with the allocator stored in the list.
  - After this call, the list is deinitialized and must not be used until it
    is initialized again.
  - A null list or a list without an allocator is left unchanged.
items.summary: Releases a directory listing and all storage owned by it.

items.name: does_path_exist
items.comment:
Reports whether a filesystem entry exists at a path.

Parameters:
  path_value : string - borrowed filesystem path to query.

Returns:
  bool - true when the entry exists; otherwise false.
items.summary: Reports whether a filesystem entry exists at a path.

items.name: is_file
items.comment:
Reports whether a path resolves to a regular file.

Parameters:
  path_value : string - borrowed filesystem path to query.

Returns:
  bool - true when metadata lookup succeeds and the entry is a regular
         file; otherwise false.
items.summary: Reports whether a path resolves to a regular file.

items.name: is_dir
items.comment:
Reports whether a path resolves to a directory.

Parameters:
  path_value : string - borrowed filesystem path to query.

Returns:
  bool - true when metadata lookup succeeds and the entry is a directory;
         otherwise false.
items.summary: Reports whether a path resolves to a directory.

items.name: create_dir_all
items.comment:
Creates a directory and any missing parent directories in its path.

Parameters:
  path_value : string - borrowed filesystem path to create.

Returns:
  FsStatus - FsStatus.Ok when the directory exists after the operation, or
             an error status when validation, allocation, or creation fails.

Notes:
  - Returns FsStatus.Ok when the path already names a directory.
  - Returns FsStatus.NotDirectory when the path already names another entry
    type.
  - Temporary path storage is allocated and released internally.
items.summary: Creates a directory and any missing parent directories in its path.

items.name: remove_file
items.comment:
Removes the filesystem entry at a path using file-removal semantics.

Parameters:
  path_value : string - borrowed filesystem path to remove.

Returns:
  FsStatus - operation status mapped from the underlying OS result.
items.summary: Removes the filesystem entry at a path using file-removal semantics.

items.name: list_dir
items.comment:
Lists the direct entries in a directory using the context allocator.

Parameters:
  path : string - borrowed path of the directory to list.

Returns:
  [containers.ArrayList<DirEntry>, FsStatus]
    - On success: a context-allocator-owned list and FsStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: an empty list that owns no storage and an error status.

Notes:
  - Returns FsStatus.InvalidAllocator when context.allocator is null.
  - The caller owns every DirEntry.name, every DirEntry.path, and the
    ArrayList backing buffer in a successful result.
  - Release a successful result with DeinitDirEntries.
  - Entry classification does not follow symbolic links or Windows
    directory links; link flags are preserved and is_dir remains false for
    links.
  - The special `.` and `..` entries are omitted.
items.summary: Lists the direct entries in a directory using the context allocator.

items.name: list_dir
items.comment:
Lists the direct entries in a directory.

Parameters:
  path_value : string     - borrowed path of the directory to list.
  allocator  : ^Allocator - allocator used for entry strings and list
                            storage. Must be non-null.

Returns:
  [containers.ArrayList<DirEntry>, FsStatus]
    - On success: an allocator-owned list and FsStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: an empty list that owns no storage and an error status.

Notes:
  - The caller owns every DirEntry.name, every DirEntry.path, and the
    ArrayList backing buffer in a successful result.
  - Release a successful result with DeinitDirEntries.
  - Entry classification does not follow symbolic links or Windows
    directory links; link flags are preserved and is_dir remains false for
    links.
  - The special `.` and `..` entries are omitted.
items.summary: Lists the direct entries in a directory.

items.name: remove_dir_all
items.comment:
Recursively removes a directory tree without traversing link targets.

Parameters:
  path_value : string - borrowed path of the directory tree to remove.

Returns:
  FsStatus - FsStatus.Ok when the entry and its descendants are removed, or
             the first error status encountered.

Notes:
  - Symbolic links are unlinked with remove_file.
  - Windows directory links and junctions are removed with remove_dir.
  - Link targets are never recursively visited.
  - Temporary traversal storage is allocated and released internally.
items.summary: Recursively removes a directory tree without traversing link targets.

items.name: copy_file
items.signature: copy_file : func(from : string, to : string) -> FsStatus
items.comment:
Copies the contents of a regular source file to a destination path.

Parameters:
  from : string - borrowed path of the source file.
  to   : string - borrowed path of the destination file.

Returns:
  FsStatus - FsStatus.Ok when the copy completes, FsStatus.SameFile when
             both paths identify the same file, or an error status.

Notes:
  - The source is validated before the destination is opened.
  - The destination is opened without truncation, compared against the
    source by opened-handle identity, and truncated only after the files are
    proven distinct.
  - Same spelling, symbolic-link aliases, and hard-link aliases return
    FsStatus.SameFile without changing file contents.
items.summary: Copies the contents of a regular source file to a destination path.

items.name: join_path
items.signature: join_path : func(a : string, b : string, allocator : ^Allocator) -> string
items.comment:
Joins two path values into a newly allocated, NUL-terminated string.

Parameters:
  a         : string     - borrowed base path.
  b         : string     - borrowed path to append.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for the returned string. Must be
                           non-null.

Returns:
  string - allocator-owned joined path, or an empty string when an argument
           is invalid or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and the
    supplied allocator.
  - When exactly one input is empty, the result is an allocated copy of the
    other value. Two empty inputs return an empty string.
  - When `b` begins with a path separator, it replaces `a`.
  - Inserts `/` only when `a` does not already end with a path separator.
  - This function joins path text without normalizing it.
items.summary: Joins two path values into a newly allocated, NUL-terminated string.

items.name: join_path
items.signature: join_path : func(a : string, b : string) -> string
items.comment:
Joins two path values using the context allocator.

Parameters:
  a : string - borrowed base path.
  b : string - borrowed path to append.

Returns:
  string - context-allocator-owned joined path, or an empty string when an
           argument is invalid or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Requires context.allocator to be non-null.
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and
    context.allocator.
items.summary: Joins two path values using the context allocator.

items.name: join_path
items.signature: join_path : func(a : string, b : string, c : string) -> string
items.comment:
Joins three path values using the context allocator.

Parameters:
  a : string - borrowed base path.
  b : string - borrowed second path component.
  c : string - borrowed third path component.

Returns:
  string - context-allocator-owned, NUL-terminated joined path, or an empty
           string when all inputs are empty, an input is invalid, the result
           is too large, or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Requires context.allocator to be non-null.
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and
    the allocator used by context.allocator for this call.
  - Allocates only the returned string; no intermediate strings are created.
  - Empty components are skipped.
  - Each join inserts `/` only when the preceding path does not already
    end with a path separator.
  - A component beginning with a path separator replaces the preceding
    path.
  - This function joins path text without normalizing it.
items.summary: Joins three path values using the context allocator.

items.name: join_path
items.signature: join_path : func(a : string, b : string, c : string, allocator : ^Allocator) -> string
items.comment:
Joins three path values using a caller-provided allocator.

Parameters:
  a         : string     - borrowed base path.
  b         : string     - borrowed second path component.
  c         : string     - borrowed third path component.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for the returned string. Must be
                           non-null.

Returns:
  string - allocator-owned, NUL-terminated joined path, or an empty string
           when all inputs are empty, an input or allocator is invalid,
           the result is too large, or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and the
    supplied allocator.
  - Allocates only the returned string; no intermediate strings are created.
  - Empty components are skipped.
  - Each join inserts `/` only when the preceding path does not already
    end with a path separator.
  - A component beginning with a path separator replaces the preceding
    path.
  - This function joins path text without normalizing it.
items.summary: Joins three path values using a caller-provided allocator.

items.name: parent
items.comment:
Copies the parent portion of a path into a newly allocated,
NUL-terminated string.

Parameters:
  value     : string     - borrowed path to inspect.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for the returned string. Must be
                           non-null.

Returns:
  string - allocator-owned parent path, or an empty string when the path is
           empty, has no parent, the allocator is null, or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Trailing path separators are ignored except for a root separator.
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and the
    supplied allocator.
items.summary: Copies the parent portion of a path into a newly allocated, NUL-terminated string.

items.name: parent
items.comment:
Copies the parent portion of a path using the context allocator.

Parameters:
  value : string - borrowed path to inspect.

Returns:
  string - context-allocator-owned parent path, or an empty string when the
           path has no parent or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Requires context.allocator to be non-null.
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and
    context.allocator.
items.summary: Copies the parent portion of a path using the context allocator.

items.name: get_filename
items.comment:
Copies the final component of a path into a newly allocated,
NUL-terminated string.

Parameters:
  path      : string     - borrowed path to inspect.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for the returned string. Must be
                           non-null.

Returns:
  string - allocator-owned final component, or an empty string when the path
           is empty, the allocator is null, or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Trailing path separators are ignored except for a root separator.
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and the
    supplied allocator.
items.summary: Copies the final component of a path into a newly allocated, NUL-terminated string.

items.name: get_filename
items.comment:
Copies the final component of a path using the context allocator.

Parameters:
  value : string - borrowed path to inspect.

Returns:
  string - context-allocator-owned final component, or an empty string when
           the path is empty or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Requires context.allocator to be non-null.
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and
    context.allocator.
items.summary: Copies the final component of a path using the context allocator.

items.name: extension
items.comment:
Copies the final component's extension into a newly allocated,
NUL-terminated string.

Parameters:
  value     : string     - borrowed path to inspect.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for the returned string. Must be
                           non-null.

Returns:
  string - allocator-owned extension including its leading `.`, or an empty
           string when the path is empty, no extension exists, the allocator
           is null, or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Trailing path separators are ignored.
  - A leading dot on the final component does not by itself count as an
    extension.
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and the
    supplied allocator.
items.summary: Copies the final component's extension into a newly allocated, NUL-terminated string.

items.name: extension
items.comment:
Copies the final component's extension using the context allocator.

Parameters:
  value : string - borrowed path to inspect.

Returns:
  string - context-allocator-owned extension including its leading `.`, or
           an empty string when no extension exists or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Requires context.allocator to be non-null.
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and
    context.allocator.
items.summary: Copies the final component's extension using the context allocator.

items.name: normalize
items.comment:
Normalizes path separators and components into a newly allocated,
NUL-terminated string.

Parameters:
  value     : string     - borrowed path to normalize.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for temporary storage and the
                           returned string. Must be non-null.

Returns:
  string - allocator-owned normalized path, or an empty string when an
           argument is invalid or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Converts path separators to `/` in the result.
  - Removes empty and `.` components and resolves `..` components.
  - An absolute path cannot ascend above its root; leading `..` components
    are preserved for relative paths.
  - An empty relative result is represented as `.`.
  - The caller must release a non-empty result with free_string and the
    supplied allocator.
items.summary: Normalizes path separators and components into a newly allocated, NUL-terminated string.

items.name: absolute
items.comment:
Produces a normalized absolute path in newly allocated storage.

Parameters:
  value     : string     - borrowed path to resolve.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for temporary storage and the
                           returned string. Must be non-null.

Returns:
  [string, IoStatus]
    - On success: an allocator-owned absolute path and IoStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: an empty string and IoStatus.InvalidAllocator when
      `allocator` is null.
    - On failure: an empty string and IoStatus.AllocatorFailed when path
      allocation fails.
    - Errors from querying the current directory are mapped to IoStatus.

Notes:
  - Absolute input is normalized directly.
  - Relative input is joined to the current directory before normalization.
  - The caller must release a successful result with free_string and the
    supplied allocator.
items.summary: Produces a normalized absolute path in newly allocated storage.

items.name: parse
items.comment:
Parses one complete JSON document from a string.

Parameters:
  source : string - JSON text to parse. The source is borrowed and remains
                    owned by the caller.

Returns:
  [JsonValue, JsonStatus] - parsed value and status. On success returns the
                            value with JsonStatus.Ok. On failure returns an
                            empty JsonValue and the status describing the
                            parse or allocation error.

Notes:
  - Strings, arrays, and objects in the returned tree are allocated with
    the current context allocator.
  - The caller owns a successful result and must call deinit with the same
    allocator.
  - Non-whitespace content after the root value returns
    JsonStatus.TrailingCharacters.
items.summary: Parses one complete JSON document from a string.

items.name: deinit
items.comment:
Recursively releases allocator-owned storage inside a JsonValue tree using
the context allocator.

Parameters:
  value : ^JsonValue - root value to clean up. May be null.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - context.allocator must match the allocator used to construct the tree.
  - This releases nested strings, arrays, objects, property keys, and child
    values, then resets the root to JsonTypeKind.Null.
  - This does not free the JsonValue object pointed to by `value`.
  - A null value or context allocator is treated as a no-op.
items.summary: Recursively releases allocator-owned storage inside a JsonValue tree using the context allocator.

items.name: deinit
items.comment:
Recursively releases allocator-owned storage inside a JsonValue tree.

Parameters:
  value     : ^JsonValue - root value to clean up. May be null.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator that owns the tree's strings and
                           container storage.

Returns:
  void

Notes:
  - The allocator must match the allocator used to construct the tree.
  - This releases nested strings, arrays, objects, property keys, and child
    values, then resets the root to JsonTypeKind.Null.
  - This does not free the JsonValue object pointed to by `value`.
  - A null value or allocator is treated as a no-op.
items.summary: Recursively releases allocator-owned storage inside a JsonValue tree.

items.name: find
items.comment:
Finds an object property using a dot-separated path such as `a.b.c`.

Parameters:
  value : ^JsonValue - root value to search. Each traversed value must be a
                       JSON object.
  name  : string     - exact, case-sensitive property path.

Returns:
  ^JsonProperty - pointer to the matching property, or null when the input
                  is invalid, a path segment is absent, or traversal reaches
                  a value that is not an object.

Notes:
  - The returned pointer aliases the JsonValue tree; no allocation or copy
    is performed.
  - The pointer becomes invalid after deinit or after the containing
    object's property list reallocates.
items.summary: Finds an object property using a dot-separated path such as `a.b.c`.

items.name: save_json
items.comment:
Serializes a JsonValue tree and writes it to a file.

Parameters:
  value : ^JsonValue - root value to serialize. The value is borrowed.
  path  : string     - destination file path.

Returns:
  JsonStatus - JsonStatus.Ok after the complete document is written and
               flushed. Returns JsonStatus.InvalidValue,
               JsonStatus.InvalidAllocator, JsonStatus.AllocationFailed,
               JsonStatus.SerializationFailed, or JsonStatus.IoError when
               the corresponding operation fails.

Notes:
  - The destination file is created or overwritten.
  - Temporary serialization storage uses the current context allocator.
  - The input tree is not consumed or modified.
items.summary: Serializes a JsonValue tree and writes it to a file.

items.name: new_value
items.comment:
Allocates storage for one JsonValue and sets its active kind.

Parameters:
  kind : JsonTypeKind - kind assigned to the new value.

Returns:
  ^JsonValue - allocated value, or null when allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Storage is allocated with the current context allocator.
  - The selected union payload must be initialized by the caller before it
    is read or passed to deinit.
  - deinit releases nested storage but not this outer allocation. The caller
    must free or delete the returned pointer separately with the same
    allocator.
items.summary: Allocates storage for one JsonValue and sets its active kind.
