items.name: ArenaAllocator
items.signature: ArenaAllocator : func( size_per_block : i64, num_block : i32 ) -> ^Allocator
items.comment:
Constructs an arena allocator from equally sized, preallocated blocks.

Parameters:
  size_per_block : i64 - size in bytes of each backing block. Must be positive.
  num_block      : i32 - number of backing blocks to allocate.

Returns:
  ^Allocator - allocator wrapper for the arena, or null when the size is invalid
               or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - A non-positive block count is normalized to one block.
  - Individual allocations are reclaimed by `clear` or `destroy`, not `free`.
items.summary: Constructs an arena allocator from equally sized, preallocated blocks.

items.name: DestroyArenaAllocator
items.comment:
Releases an arena allocator's block metadata and concrete policy object.

Parameters:
  alloc : ^^ArenaAllocator - pointer to the concrete arena policy pointer.

Returns:
  MemoryStatus - MemoryStatus.Ok when the policy was released;
                 MemoryStatus.Error when no policy was supplied.

Notes:
  - This low-level helper does not release the individual block buffers.
  - Prefer `Allocator.destroy()` while the arena still owns its block buffers.
items.summary: Releases an arena allocator's block metadata and concrete policy object.

items.name: arena_allocator_alloc
items.signature: arena_allocator_alloc : func(alloc_data : RawPtr, op : AllocatorOp, size : i64, alignment : i64, ptr : RawPtr ) -> [RawPtr, MemoryStatus]
items.comment:
Dispatches an allocator operation to a concrete arena policy.

Parameters:
  alloc_data : RawPtr      - concrete ArenaAllocator policy pointer.
  op         : AllocatorOp - operation to perform.
  size       : i64         - requested allocation size in bytes.
  alignment  : i64         - requested allocation alignment in bytes.
  ptr        : RawPtr      - allocation supplied to a free operation.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - operation result pointer and status.

Notes:
  - This context-free function is suitable for use as `Allocator.alloc_fn`.
items.summary: Dispatches an allocator operation to a concrete arena policy.

items.name: allocate_aligned
items.signature: allocate_aligned : func(self : ^ArenaAllocator, size : i64, alignment : i64) -> [RawPtr, MemoryStatus]
items.comment:
Reserves aligned storage from the current or next available arena block.

Parameters:
  self      : ^ArenaAllocator - arena policy to allocate from.
  size      : i64             - number of bytes to reserve. Must be positive.
  alignment : i64             - requested power-of-two alignment in bytes.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - aligned allocation and MemoryStatus.Ok on success;
                           MemoryStatus.Error for invalid arguments; or
                           MemoryStatus.OutOfMemory when no block can fit it.

Notes:
  - An alignment of zero requests one-byte alignment.
  - Existing allocations remain valid until the arena is cleared or destroyed.
items.summary: Reserves aligned storage from the current or next available arena block.

items.name: allocate
items.comment:
Reserves storage from an arena using the default allocator alignment.

Parameters:
  self : ^ArenaAllocator - arena policy to allocate from.
  size : i64             - number of bytes to reserve. Must be positive.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - allocation result and status.
items.summary: Reserves storage from an arena using the default allocator alignment.

items.name: free
items.comment:
Accepts an individual arena allocation without reclaiming its storage.

Parameters:
  self : ^ArenaAllocator - arena policy associated with the allocation.
  ptr  : RawPtr         - allocation passed through unchanged.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - the supplied pointer and MemoryStatus.Ok.

Notes:
  - Arena allocations are reclaimed together by `clear` or `destroy`.
items.summary: Accepts an individual arena allocation without reclaiming its storage.

items.name: clear
items.comment:
Resets every arena block for reuse and selects the first block as current.

Parameters:
  self : ^ArenaAllocator - initialized arena policy to reset.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok.

Notes:
  - Existing pointers may be overwritten by subsequent allocations.
items.summary: Resets every arena block for reuse and selects the first block as current.

items.name: destroy
items.comment:
Releases every arena block, its metadata, and the concrete policy object.

Parameters:
  self : ^ArenaAllocator - initialized arena policy to destroy.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok.

Notes:
  - The arena policy and all allocations from it are invalid after this call.
items.summary: Releases every arena block, its metadata, and the concrete policy object.

items.name: HeapAllocator
items.comment:
Constructs an allocator backed by the process heap.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  ^Allocator - allocator wrapper whose allocations can be freed individually.
items.summary: Constructs an allocator backed by the process heap.

items.name: DestroyHeapAllocator
items.comment:
Releases a concrete heap allocator policy object.

Parameters:
  alloc : ^^HeapAllocator - pointer to the concrete heap policy pointer.

Returns:
  MemoryStatus - MemoryStatus.Ok when the policy was released;
                 MemoryStatus.Error when no policy was supplied.

Notes:
  - Outstanding heap allocations must be freed separately.
items.summary: Releases a concrete heap allocator policy object.

items.name: allocate_aligned
items.signature: allocate_aligned : func(self : ^HeapAllocator, size : i64, alignment : i64) -> [RawPtr, MemoryStatus]
items.comment:
Allocates storage from the process heap with a requested alignment.

Parameters:
  self      : ^HeapAllocator - heap policy to allocate from.
  size      : i64            - number of bytes to allocate. Must be positive.
  alignment : i64            - requested power-of-two alignment in bytes.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - aligned allocation and MemoryStatus.Ok on success;
                           MemoryStatus.Error for invalid arguments; or
                           MemoryStatus.OutOfMemory when allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Alignments smaller than the default allocator alignment are promoted to it.
  - A private header retains the original `malloc` pointer for `free`.
items.summary: Allocates storage from the process heap with a requested alignment.

items.name: allocate
items.comment:
Allocates storage from the process heap using the default allocator alignment.

Parameters:
  self : ^HeapAllocator - heap policy to allocate from.
  size : i64            - number of bytes to allocate. Must be positive.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - allocation result and status.
items.summary: Allocates storage from the process heap using the default allocator alignment.

items.name: clear
items.comment:
Performs the allocator-wide clear operation without releasing heap allocations.

Parameters:
  self : ^HeapAllocator - heap policy to clear.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok.

Notes:
  - Heap allocations remain individually owned, so this operation is a no-op.
items.summary: Performs the allocator-wide clear operation without releasing heap allocations.

items.name: free
items.comment:
Releases an allocation produced by this heap allocator.

Parameters:
  self : ^HeapAllocator - heap policy associated with the allocation.
  ptr  : RawPtr        - non-null allocation to release.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok on success, or null and
                           MemoryStatus.Error for an invalid pointer.
items.summary: Releases an allocation produced by this heap allocator.

items.name: destroy
items.comment:
Releases the concrete heap allocator policy object.

Parameters:
  self : ^HeapAllocator - heap policy to destroy.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok.

Notes:
  - Outstanding heap allocations must be freed separately before this call.
items.summary: Releases the concrete heap allocator policy object.

items.name: PermanentAllocator
items.comment:
Constructs a permanent allocator with an initial backing block.

Parameters:
  buffer_size : i64 - initial block size in bytes. Must be positive.

Returns:
  ^Allocator - allocator wrapper for the permanent policy, or null when the
               size is invalid or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Additional, progressively larger blocks are appended as needed.
  - Individual allocations are reclaimed by `clear` or `destroy`, not `free`.
items.summary: Constructs a permanent allocator with an initial backing block.

items.name: DestroyPermanentAllocator
items.comment:
Releases a concrete permanent allocator and all of its backing blocks.

Parameters:
  alloc : ^^PermanentAllocator - pointer to the concrete permanent policy pointer.

Returns:
  MemoryStatus - MemoryStatus.Ok when the policy was released;
                 MemoryStatus.Error when no policy was supplied.

Notes:
  - The concrete policy pointer is set to null after successful destruction.
items.summary: Releases a concrete permanent allocator and all of its backing blocks.

items.name: permanent_allocator_alloc
items.signature: permanent_allocator_alloc : func(alloc_data : RawPtr, op : AllocatorOp, size : i64, alignment : i64, ptr : RawPtr ) -> [RawPtr, MemoryStatus]
items.comment:
Dispatches an allocator operation to a concrete permanent policy.

Parameters:
  alloc_data : RawPtr      - concrete PermanentAllocator policy pointer.
  op         : AllocatorOp - operation to perform.
  size       : i64         - requested allocation size in bytes.
  alignment  : i64         - requested allocation alignment in bytes.
  ptr        : RawPtr      - allocation supplied to a free operation.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - operation result pointer and status.

Notes:
  - This context-free function is suitable for use as `Allocator.alloc_fn`.
items.summary: Dispatches an allocator operation to a concrete permanent policy.

items.name: permanent_allocator_grow
items.comment: Appends a new backing block without moving any earlier allocation.
items.summary: Appends a new backing block without moving any earlier allocation.

items.name: allocate_aligned
items.signature: allocate_aligned : func(self : ^PermanentAllocator, size : i64, alignment : i64) -> [RawPtr, MemoryStatus]
items.comment:
Reserves aligned storage from stable, append-only backing blocks.

Parameters:
  self      : ^PermanentAllocator - permanent policy to allocate from.
  size      : i64                 - number of bytes to reserve. Must be positive.
  alignment : i64                 - requested power-of-two alignment in bytes.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - aligned allocation and MemoryStatus.Ok on success;
                           MemoryStatus.Error for invalid arguments; or
                           MemoryStatus.OutOfMemory when growth fails.

Notes:
  - An alignment of zero requests one-byte alignment.
  - New blocks are appended when necessary; existing allocations never move.
items.summary: Reserves aligned storage from stable, append-only backing blocks.

items.name: allocate
items.comment:
Reserves storage from a permanent allocator using the default alignment.

Parameters:
  self : ^PermanentAllocator - permanent policy to allocate from.
  size : i64                 - number of bytes to reserve. Must be positive.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - allocation result and status.
items.summary: Reserves storage from a permanent allocator using the default alignment.

items.name: free
items.comment:
Accepts an individual permanent allocation without reclaiming its storage.

Parameters:
  self : ^PermanentAllocator - permanent policy associated with the allocation.
  ptr  : RawPtr             - allocation accepted for API compatibility.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok.

Notes:
  - Permanent allocations are reclaimed together by `clear` or `destroy`.
items.summary: Accepts an individual permanent allocation without reclaiming its storage.

items.name: clear
items.comment:
Resets every backing block for reuse and selects the first block as current.

Parameters:
  self : ^PermanentAllocator - initialized permanent policy to reset.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok on success, or null and
                           MemoryStatus.Error for an invalid policy.

Notes:
  - Existing pointers may be overwritten by subsequent allocations.
items.summary: Resets every backing block for reuse and selects the first block as current.

items.name: destroy
items.comment:
Releases every backing block and the concrete permanent policy object.

Parameters:
  self : ^PermanentAllocator - permanent policy to destroy.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok on success, or null and
                           MemoryStatus.Error for an invalid policy.

Notes:
  - The policy and all allocations from it are invalid after this call.
items.summary: Releases every backing block and the concrete permanent policy object.

items.name: PoolAllocator
items.comment:
Constructs a fixed-capacity pool for equally sized allocations using the
default allocator alignment.

Parameters:
  block_size  : i64 - maximum allocation size in bytes for one pool slot.
  block_count : i64 - number of slots owned by the pool.

Returns:
  ^Allocator - allocator wrapper for the pool, or null when an argument is
               invalid or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Every successful allocation consumes exactly one slot.
  - Individual slots can be returned to the pool with `free`.
items.summary: Constructs a fixed-capacity pool for equally sized allocations using the default allocator alignment.

items.name: PoolAllocator
items.signature: PoolAllocator : func(block_size : i64, block_count : i64, alignment : i64) -> ^Allocator
items.comment:
Constructs a fixed-capacity pool for equally sized allocations with an
explicit alignment.

Parameters:
  block_size  : i64 - maximum allocation size in bytes for one pool slot.
  block_count : i64 - number of slots owned by the pool.
  alignment   : i64 - requested power-of-two slot alignment in bytes.

Returns:
  ^Allocator - allocator wrapper for the pool, or null when an argument is
               invalid or allocation fails.

Notes:
  - Zero alignment follows allocator normalization and is promoted to the
    default allocator alignment.
  - Alignments smaller than the default allocator alignment are promoted to it.
items.summary: Constructs a fixed-capacity pool for equally sized allocations with an explicit alignment.

items.name: DestroyPoolAllocator
items.comment:
Releases a concrete pool allocator and all storage owned by it.

Parameters:
  alloc : ^^PoolAllocator - pointer to the concrete pool policy pointer.

Returns:
  MemoryStatus - MemoryStatus.Ok when the policy was released;
                 MemoryStatus.Error when no policy was supplied.

Notes:
  - The concrete policy pointer is set to null after successful destruction.
  - An Allocator wrapper that referenced the policy remains caller-owned.
items.summary: Releases a concrete pool allocator and all storage owned by it.

items.name: allocate_aligned
items.signature: allocate_aligned : func(self : ^PoolAllocator, size : i64, alignment : i64) -> [RawPtr, MemoryStatus]
items.comment:
Reserves one free pool slot with a requested alignment.

Parameters:
  self      : ^PoolAllocator - initialized pool policy to allocate from.
  size      : i64            - requested size in bytes.
  alignment : i64            - requested power-of-two alignment in bytes.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - slot pointer and MemoryStatus.Ok on success;
                           MemoryStatus.Error for an invalid request; or
                           MemoryStatus.OutOfMemory when every slot is in use.

Notes:
  - The requested size cannot exceed the configured block size.
  - The requested alignment cannot exceed the pool's configured alignment.
  - Zero alignment follows allocator normalization and requests one-byte alignment.
items.summary: Reserves one free pool slot with a requested alignment.

items.name: allocate
items.comment:
Reserves one free pool slot using the default allocator alignment.

Parameters:
  self : ^PoolAllocator - initialized pool policy to allocate from.
  size : i64            - requested size in bytes.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - allocation result and status.
items.summary: Reserves one free pool slot using the default allocator alignment.

items.name: free
items.comment:
Returns one live slot to the pool.

Parameters:
  self : ^PoolAllocator - initialized pool policy that owns the slot.
  ptr  : RawPtr        - exact start address of a live pool slot.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok on success, or null and
                           MemoryStatus.Error for a null, foreign, interior,
                           or already-free pointer.
items.summary: Returns one live slot to the pool.

items.name: clear
items.comment:
Returns every slot to the pool and rebuilds its free list.

Parameters:
  self : ^PoolAllocator - initialized pool policy to reset.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok on success, or null and
                           MemoryStatus.Error for an invalid policy.

Notes:
  - Every outstanding allocation becomes invalid after this call.
items.summary: Returns every slot to the pool and rebuilds its free list.

items.name: destroy
items.comment:
Releases the pool's usage map, backing allocation, and concrete policy.

Parameters:
  self : ^PoolAllocator - initialized pool policy to destroy.

Returns:
  [RawPtr, MemoryStatus] - null and MemoryStatus.Ok on success, or null and
                           MemoryStatus.Error for an invalid policy.

Notes:
  - The Allocator wrapper remains caller-owned and must not be used afterward.
items.summary: Releases the pool's usage map, backing allocation, and concrete policy.

items.name: pool_allocator_rebuild_free_list
items.comment: Clears the usage map and links every slot into the intrusive free list.
items.summary: Clears the usage map and links every slot into the intrusive free list.

items.name: pool_allocator_slot_index
items.comment: Computes a slot index only for pointers that identify an exact slot start.
items.summary: Computes a slot index only for pointers that identify an exact slot start.

items.name: dns_resolve
items.signature: dns_resolve : func(host : string, port : u32, allocator : ^Allocator) -> [containers.ArrayList<DnsRecord>, DnsStatus]
items.comment:
Resolves a host and numeric port into connect-ready DNS records.

Parameters:
  host      : string     - DNS name or numeric address. Must not be empty.
  port      : u32        - port in host byte order.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used by the returned ArrayList.

Returns:
  [ArrayList<DnsRecord>, DnsStatus]
    - On success: one or more DNS records and DnsStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: an empty or partial list and the matching DnsStatus.

Notes:
  - The caller owns the returned list and should call DeinitArrayList(&records) when done.
  - Use the service overload when a named service such as "https" is needed.
items.summary: Resolves a host and numeric port into connect-ready DNS records.

items.name: dns_resolve
items.signature: dns_resolve : func(host : string, service : string, hints : DnsHints, allocator : ^Allocator) -> [containers.ArrayList<DnsRecord>, DnsStatus]
items.comment:
Resolves a host and service using explicit DNS hints.

Parameters:
  host      : string     - DNS name or numeric address. Must not be empty
                           unless DnsHints.passive is true.
  service   : string     - service name or numeric service, such as "443".
  hints     : DnsHints   - address family, socket type, protocol, and flags.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used by the returned ArrayList.

Returns:
  [ArrayList<DnsRecord>, DnsStatus]
    - On success: one or more DNS records and DnsStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: an empty or partial list and the matching DnsStatus.

Notes:
  - The caller owns the returned list and should call DeinitArrayList(&records) when done.
items.summary: Resolves a host and service using explicit DNS hints.

items.name: dns_resolve_ip
items.comment:
Resolves a host into IP addresses.

Parameters:
  host      : string     - DNS name or numeric address. Must not be empty.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used by the returned ArrayList.

Returns:
  [ArrayList<IPAddress>, DnsStatus]
    - On success: one or more IP addresses and DnsStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: an empty or partial list and the matching DnsStatus.

Notes:
  - The caller owns the returned list and should call DeinitArrayList(&ips) when done.
items.summary: Resolves a host into IP addresses.

items.name: connect_socket
items.comment:
Opens and connects a socket using a DNS record.

Parameters:
  record : DnsRecord - DNS result containing address, socket type, and protocol.

Returns:
  [Socket, NetStatus]
    - On success: connected Socket and NetStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: empty Socket and the matching NetStatus.

Notes:
  - The caller owns the returned socket and should call close when done.
items.summary: Opens and connects a socket using a DNS record.

items.name: dns_connect
items.signature: dns_connect : func(host : string, port : u32, allocator : ^Allocator) -> [Socket, NetStatus]
items.comment:
Resolves a host and connects to the first reachable DNS record.

Parameters:
  host      : string     - DNS name or numeric address. Must not be empty.
  port      : u32        - port in host byte order.
  allocator : ^Allocator - allocator used for the temporary DNS record list.

Returns:
  [Socket, NetStatus]
    - On success: connected Socket and NetStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: empty Socket and the matching NetStatus.

Notes:
  - The temporary DNS record list is released before returning.
  - The caller owns the returned socket and should call close when done.
items.summary: Resolves a host and connects to the first reachable DNS record.

items.name: parse_ip
items.comment:
Parses a numeric IPv4 or IPv6 string into an IPAddress.

Parameters:
  str : string - address text, such as "127.0.0.1", "::1", or
                 "2001:db8::1".

Returns:
  [IPAddress, NetStatus]
    - On success: parsed IPAddress and NetStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: empty IPAddress and NetStatus.InvalidAddress.

Notes:
  - This parses numeric addresses only. DNS names should go through a DNS
    resolver API.
items.summary: Parses a numeric IPv4 or IPv6 string into an IPAddress.

items.name: SocketAddress
items.signature: SocketAddress : func(address : IPAddress, port : u32) -> [SocketAddress, NetStatus]
items.comment:
Builds a socket address from an IP address and port.

Parameters:
  address : IPAddress - IPv4 or IPv6 address.
  port    : u32       - port in host byte order.

Returns:
  [SocketAddress, NetStatus]
    - On success: the address and NetStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: an empty address and NetStatus.InvalidAddress.
items.summary: Builds a socket address from an IP address and port.

items.name: connect_socket
items.signature: connect_socket : func(address : IPAddress, port : u32, socket_type : SocketType, protocol : Protocol) -> [Socket, NetStatus]
items.comment:
Opens and connects a native socket to the given IP address and port.

Parameters:
  address     : IPAddress  - remote IP address.
  port        : u32        - remote TCP or UDP port in host byte order.
  socket_type : SocketType - stream or datagram socket.
  protocol    : Protocol   - protocol hint; Protocol.Default lets the OS choose.

Returns:
  [Socket, NetStatus]
    - On success: the connected Socket and NetStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: an empty Socket and the matching NetStatus.

Notes:
  - This is the client-side convenience helper. Use Socket.open when you need
    an unconnected socket.
  - The caller owns the returned socket and should call close when done.
items.summary: Opens and connects a native socket to the given IP address and port.

items.name: open
items.signature: open : func(self : ^TcpListener, address : ^IPAddress, port : u32, backlog : i32) -> NetStatus
items.comment:
Opens, binds, and listens on a TCP socket.

Parameters:
  address : ^IPAddress - local IPv4 or IPv6 address to bind.
  port    : u32        - local port in host byte order. Use 0 to ask the
                         OS for an ephemeral port.
  backlog : i32        - listen backlog passed to the native socket API.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, or the matching NetStatus on failure.

Notes:
  - Address reuse is enabled before binding.
  - The caller owns the listener and should call close when done.
items.summary: Opens, binds, and listens on a TCP socket.

items.name: is_open
items.comment: Reports whether this listener currently owns a native socket handle.
items.summary: Reports whether this listener currently owns a native socket handle.

items.name: accept
items.comment:
Accepts the next incoming TCP connection.

Returns:
  [Socket, SocketAddress, NetStatus]
    - On success: accepted client socket, peer address, and NetStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: empty values and the matching NetStatus.
items.summary: Accepts the next incoming TCP connection.

items.name: close
items.comment:
Closes the listener socket.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null or closed
  listener, or NetStatus.SocketFailed when native close fails.
items.summary: Closes the listener socket.

items.name: open
items.signature: open : func(self : ^Socket, address : IPAddress, socket_type : SocketType, protocol : Protocol) -> NetStatus
items.comment:
Opens this Socket using the family stored in `address`.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidAddress for an unspecified
  address family, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null receiver, or
  NetStatus.SocketFailed when the native socket call fails.
items.summary: Opens this Socket using the family stored in `address`.

items.name: close
items.comment:
Closes this socket handle.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null or already
  invalid socket, or NetStatus.SocketFailed when the native close fails.
items.summary: Closes this socket handle.

items.name: is_open
items.comment: Reports whether this Socket currently owns a native handle.
items.summary: Reports whether this Socket currently owns a native handle.

items.name: connect
items.signature: connect : func(self : ^Socket, address : IPAddress, port : u32) -> NetStatus
items.comment:
Connects this socket to an IP address and port.

Parameters:
  self    : ^Socket   - open socket to connect.
  address : IPAddress - remote IP address.
  port    : u32       - remote TCP or UDP port in host byte order.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null or closed
  socket, NetStatus.InvalidAddress for an unsupported address family or
  family mismatch, or NetStatus.ConnectFailed when native connect fails.
items.summary: Connects this socket to an IP address and port.

items.name: connect
items.comment:
Connects this socket to a socket address.

Parameters:
  self    : ^Socket       - open socket to connect.
  address : SocketAddress - remote address and port. The port is in host
                            byte order and is converted before calling
                            the native API.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null or closed
  socket, NetStatus.InvalidAddress for an unsupported address family or
  family mismatch, or NetStatus.ConnectFailed when native connect fails.
items.summary: Connects this socket to a socket address.

items.name: set_reuse_address
items.comment:
Enables or disables address reuse on this socket.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null or closed
  socket, or NetStatus.SocketFailed when the native option call fails.
items.summary: Enables or disables address reuse on this socket.

items.name: bind
items.signature: bind : func(self : ^Socket, address : IPAddress, port : u32) -> NetStatus
items.comment:
Binds this socket to an IP address and port.

Parameters:
  address : IPAddress - local IPv4 or IPv6 address.
  port    : u32       - local port in host byte order. Use 0 to ask the
                        OS for an ephemeral port.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null or closed
  socket, NetStatus.InvalidAddress for invalid address data, or
  NetStatus.BindFailed when native bind fails.
items.summary: Binds this socket to an IP address and port.

items.name: bind
items.comment:
Binds this socket to a socket address.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null or closed
  socket, NetStatus.InvalidAddress for invalid address data, or
  NetStatus.BindFailed when native bind fails.
items.summary: Binds this socket to a socket address.

items.name: listen
items.comment:
Marks this socket as a passive listening socket.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null or closed
  socket, or NetStatus.ListenFailed when native listen fails.
items.summary: Marks this socket as a passive listening socket.

items.name: accept
items.comment:
Accepts the next incoming connection.

Returns:
  [Socket, SocketAddress, NetStatus]
    - On success: accepted socket, peer address, and NetStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: empty values and the matching socket/address/status.
items.summary: Accepts the next incoming connection.

items.name: shutdown
items.comment:
Disables receive, send, or both directions on this socket.

Returns:
  NetStatus.Ok on success, NetStatus.InvalidSocket for a null or closed
  socket, or NetStatus.SocketFailed when native shutdown fails.
items.summary: Disables receive, send, or both directions on this socket.

items.name: send
items.comment:
Sends bytes from `buffer` using SocketSendFlags.None.

Returns:
  [i64, NetStatus] - byte count and status.

items.name: StringBuilderDeinit
items.comment:
Frees a StringBuilder's backing storage and resets its fields.

Parameters:
  self : ^StringBuilder - builder to deinitialize. May be null.

Notes:

    to_string() remain owned by their callers.
items.summary: Frees a StringBuilder's backing storage and resets its fields.

items.name: append
items.comment:
Appends a borrowed byte range to the builder without constructing a
temporary string. The bytes are copied into the builder's owned storage.

Parameters:
  self  : ^StringBuilder - builder to mutate.
  value : []u8           - borrowed bytes to copy.

Returns:
  true when the bytes were appended or the range is valid and empty; false
  for an invalid range, integer overflow, or allocation failure.
items.summary: Appends a borrowed byte range to the builder without constructing a temporary string. The bytes are copied into the builder's owned storage.

items.name: to_string
items.comment:
Copies the builder's bytes into an independently-owned, terminated string.

Returns:

    - StringStatus.Ok for a successful copy or a valid empty builder.
    - StringStatus.InvalidArg for a null or internally invalid builder.
    - StringStatus.InvalidAllocator when the builder has no allocator.
    - StringStatus.OutOfMemory when copying non-empty contents fails.

Notes:
  - A valid empty builder returns the canonical empty string with Ok.
  - The caller owns a non-empty returned string and must release it with the
    builder's allocator.
items.summary: Copies the builder's bytes into an independently-owned, terminated string.

items.name: make_string
items.comment:
Constructs an owned string by copying the contents of a null-terminated C string.

Parameters:
  src       - Source null-terminated C string to copy. May be null.
  allocator - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string containing a copy of src. Returns an empty string
  if src is null, has zero length, or the allocation fails.

The returned string owns its buffer and must be released via free_string
using the same allocator.
items.summary: Constructs an owned string by copying the contents of a null-terminated C string.

items.name: make_string
items.comment:
Copies a null-terminated C string using context.allocator.

Parameters:
  src - Source null-terminated C string to copy. May be null.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated owned string, or an empty string when src is null,
  empty, or allocation fails. The result must be released via free_string
  using the allocator active in context when this function was called.
items.summary: Copies a null-terminated C string using context.allocator.

items.name: make_string
items.signature: make_string : func(src : ^u8, length : i64, allocator : ^Allocator) -> string
items.comment:
Constructs an owned string by copying a raw byte range.

Parameters:
  src       - Pointer to the first byte to copy. May be null.
  length    - Number of bytes to copy.
  allocator - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string containing a copy of the requested bytes.
  Returns an empty string if src is null, length is non-positive, or the
  allocation fails.

The allocation reserves one additional byte and stores a trailing zero at
data[length]. The terminator is not included in the returned string's length.

The returned string owns its buffer and must be released via free_string
using the same allocator.

This overload selects allocator in its function-scoped Context and delegates
the allocation and copy to the compiler intrinsic. The caller's Context is
restored when this function returns.
items.summary: Constructs an owned string by copying a raw byte range.

items.name: make_string
items.comment:
Allocates an uninitialized string using context.allocator.

Parameters:
  length - Number of bytes to allocate for the string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string of `length` bytes. The buffer's contents are
  undefined and must be initialized by the caller before use. One additional
  byte is allocated and initialized to zero at data[length]; the terminator
  is not included in length.

The returned string owns its buffer and must be released via free_string
using the allocator active in context when this function was called.
items.summary: Allocates an uninitialized string using context.allocator.

items.name: make_string
items.comment:
Allocates a string of the requested length with uninitialized contents.

Parameters:
  length    - Number of bytes to allocate for the string's buffer.
  allocator - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string of `length` bytes. The buffer's contents are
  undefined and must be initialized by the caller before use. One additional
  byte is allocated and initialized to zero at data[length]; the terminator
  is not included in length.

The returned string owns its buffer and must be released via free_string
using the same allocator.
items.summary: Allocates a string of the requested length with uninitialized contents.

items.name: make_string
items.comment:
Constructs an owned string by copying the contents of a byte slice.

Parameters:
  slice     - Source byte slice to copy.
  allocator - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string containing a copy of slice's bytes. Returns an
  empty string if slice.data is null, slice.length is non-positive, or the
  allocation fails.

The returned string owns its buffer and must be released via free_string
using the same allocator. The returned string does not alias the source
slice, so later changes to slice.data do not affect the returned string.
items.summary: Constructs an owned string by copying the contents of a byte slice.

items.name: make_string
items.comment:
Copies a byte slice using context.allocator.

Parameters:
  slice - Source byte slice to copy.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated owned string, or an empty string when slice is invalid,
  empty, or allocation fails. The result does not alias slice.data and must
  be released via free_string using the allocator active in context when
  this function was called.
items.summary: Copies a byte slice using context.allocator.

items.name: free_string
items.comment:
Frees the memory associated with the given string.

Parameters:
  str       - Pointer to the string to free. May be null, in which case the call is a no-op.
  allocator - Allocator used to release str.data. Must match the allocator that produced it.

On return, str.data is set to null and str.length is set to -1.
items.summary: Frees the memory associated with the given string.

items.name: free_string
items.comment:
Frees an owned string using context.allocator.

Parameters:
  str - Pointer to the string to free. May be null.

The allocator active in context must match the allocator that produced
str.data. On return, str.data is null and str.length is -1.
items.summary: Frees an owned string using context.allocator.

items.name: split
items.comment:
Splits a string into independently-owned strings.

Parameters:
  str       - Pointer to the string to split.
  delimeter - Delimiter byte to search for.
  The allocator active in context is used for both the returned ArrayList
  storage and every non-empty string element.

Returns:
  An containers.ArrayList<string> containing allocated copies of the spans between
  delimiters. Empty spans are preserved as empty strings. Returns an empty
  list when str is null, str.length is negative, a non-empty string has null
  data, context.allocator is null, or an allocation fails. A valid empty
  string produces one empty element regardless of whether its data pointer
  is null or points at a terminator.

The caller owns both levels of storage. Release each non-empty element with
free_string using the allocator active in context when split was called,
then call DeinitArrayList on the returned list.
items.summary: Splits a string into independently-owned strings.

items.name: to_bytes
items.comment:
Returns a byte-slice view over the string's contents.

Parameters:
  self - Pointer to the string to view.

Returns:
  A []u8 slice aliasing self.data with length self.length. No allocation
  or copy is performed. Use this when byte-level iteration is intended;
  plain string iteration yields char values.
items.summary: Returns a byte-slice view over the string's contents.

items.name: make_cstring
items.comment:
Copies the string into a newly-allocated, null-terminated C string.

Parameters:
  value - String to copy.

Returns:
  A malloc-allocated cstring containing value's bytes followed by a null
  terminator. Returns null if value is non-empty with null data, if value
  has a negative length, or if allocation fails. The returned pointer must
  be released with free().
items.summary: Copies the string into a newly-allocated, null-terminated C string.

items.name: to_slice
items.comment:
Returns a byte-slice view over the string's contents.

Parameters:
  self - Pointer to the string to view.

Returns:
  A []u8 slice aliasing self.data with length self.length. No allocation
  or copy is performed; the slice remains valid only as long as self.data
  is live.
items.summary: Returns a byte-slice view over the string's contents.

items.name: to_slice
items.comment:
Returns a byte-slice view over the first `len` bytes of the string.

Parameters:
  self - Pointer to the string to view.
  len  - Maximum number of bytes to include in the returned slice.

Returns:
  A []u8 slice aliasing self.data. If `len` is greater than or equal to
  self.length, the full string is returned; otherwise the slice is
  truncated to `len` bytes. No allocation or copy is performed; the slice
  remains valid only as long as self.data is live.
items.summary: Returns a byte-slice view over the first `len` bytes of the string.

items.name: clone
items.comment:
Produces an independently-allocated copy of the string.

Parameters:
  self  - Pointer to the string to copy. May be null.
  alloc - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string containing a copy of self's bytes. Returns an
  empty string if self is null, self.data is null, self.length is
  non-positive, or the allocation fails.

The returned string owns its buffer and must be released via free_string
using the same allocator.
items.summary: Produces an independently-allocated copy of the string.

items.name: clone
items.comment:
Copies the string using context.allocator.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated owned copy, or an empty string when self is null,
  empty, or allocation fails. The result must be released via free_string
  using the allocator active in context when this function was called.
items.summary: Copies the string using context.allocator.

items.name: to_upper
items.comment:
Copies the string and converts ASCII letters to uppercase.

Parameters:
  self      - Pointer to the source string. Left unchanged.
  allocator - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string with bytes `a` through `z` converted to `A`
  through `Z`. Returns an empty string when self is null, self.data is
  null, self.length is non-positive, or allocation fails.

This function performs ASCII case conversion only; it does not apply
Unicode case mappings. Non-ASCII UTF-8 sequences are copied byte-for-byte,
so `é` remains `é` and emoji remain unchanged. Valid UTF-8 input therefore
remains valid UTF-8. The returned string owns its buffer and must be
released via free_string using the same allocator.
items.summary: Copies the string and converts ASCII letters to uppercase.

items.name: to_upper
items.comment:
Copies the string and converts ASCII letters to uppercase using
context.allocator.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated owned string. This is ASCII-only; non-ASCII UTF-8
  sequences are copied unchanged and no Unicode case mapping is performed.
  The result must be released via free_string using the allocator that was
  active in context when this function was called.
items.summary: Copies the string and converts ASCII letters to uppercase using context.allocator.

items.name: to_lower
items.comment:
Copies the string and converts ASCII letters to lowercase.

Parameters:
  self      - Pointer to the source string. Left unchanged.
  allocator - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string with bytes `A` through `Z` converted to `a`
  through `z`. Returns an empty string when self is null, self.data is
  null, self.length is non-positive, or allocation fails.

This function performs ASCII case conversion only; it does not apply
Unicode case mappings. Non-ASCII UTF-8 sequences are copied byte-for-byte,
so `É` remains `É` and emoji remain unchanged. Valid UTF-8 input therefore
remains valid UTF-8. The returned string owns its buffer and must be
released via free_string using the same allocator.
items.summary: Copies the string and converts ASCII letters to lowercase.

items.name: to_lower
items.comment:
Copies the string and converts ASCII letters to lowercase using
context.allocator.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated owned string. This is ASCII-only; non-ASCII UTF-8
  sequences are copied unchanged and no Unicode case mapping is performed.
  The result must be released via free_string using the allocator that was
  active in context when this function was called.
items.summary: Copies the string and converts ASCII letters to lowercase using context.allocator.

items.name: compare
items.signature: compare : func(self : string, other : string, ignore_case : bool = false) -> bool
items.comment:
Compares two strings, optionally ignoring ASCII letter case.

Parameters:
  self        - Pointer to the first string.
  other       - Second string value.
  ignore_case - When true, ASCII letters `A` through `Z` are treated as
                equivalent to `a` through `z`.

Returns:
  true when both strings have equal lengths and matching bytes; otherwise
  false. When ignore_case is true, matching is ASCII case-insensitive;
  non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes are still compared exactly. Valid zero-length strings
  compare equal regardless of whether their data pointer is null or points at
  a terminator. No allocation is performed.
items.summary: Compares two strings, optionally ignoring ASCII letter case.

items.name: compare
items.signature: compare : func(slice : []u8, other : string, ignore_case : bool = false) -> bool
items.comment:
Compares a byte slice with a string, optionally ignoring ASCII
letter case.

Parameters:
  slice       - Byte slice to compare. Left unchanged.
  other       - String value to compare against the slice.
  ignore_case - When true, ASCII letters `A` through `Z` are treated as
                equivalent to `a` through `z`.

Returns:
  true when the slice and string have equal lengths and matching bytes;
  otherwise false. When ignore_case is true, matching is ASCII
  case-insensitive; non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes are still compared exactly.
  No allocation is performed.
items.summary: Compares a byte slice with a string, optionally ignoring ASCII letter case.

items.name: substring
items.signature: substring : func(self : ^string, start_index : i64, count : i64) -> string
items.comment:
Copies a byte range into a newly-allocated string.

Parameters:
  self     - Pointer to the string to slice.
  start_index - Zero-based byte offset where the substring begins.
  count    - Number of bytes to include.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string containing a copy of the requested byte range.
  Returns an empty string when self is null, self.data is null,
  start_index/count are negative, count is zero, the requested range
  exceeds self.length, or allocation fails.

The returned string owns its buffer and must be released via free_string.
items.summary: Copies a byte range into a newly-allocated string.

items.name: concat
items.signature: concat : func(self : ^string, s1 : string, allocator : ^Allocator ) -> string
items.comment:
Joins the string with another, producing a newly-allocated result.

Parameters:
  self      - Pointer to the leading string. Left unchanged.
  s1        - Trailing string to append after self. Left unchanged.
  allocator - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string containing self followed by s1.

The returned string owns its buffer and must be released via free_string
using the same allocator.
items.summary: Joins the string with another, producing a newly-allocated result.

items.name: concat
items.signature: concat : func(self : ^string, s1 : cstring, allocator : ^Allocator ) -> string
items.comment:
Appends a null-terminated C string to this string.

Parameters:
  self      - Pointer to the leading string. Left unchanged.
  s1        - Null-terminated C string to append.
  allocator - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated owned string containing self followed by s1. The result
  must be released via free_string using the same allocator.
items.summary: Appends a null-terminated C string to this string.

items.name: concat
items.signature: concat : func(self : ^string, s1 : string, s2 : string, allocator : ^Allocator) -> string
items.comment:
Joins the string with two others, producing a newly-allocated result.

Parameters:
  self      - Pointer to the leading string. Left unchanged.
  s1        - Second string, appended after self. Left unchanged.
  s2        - Third string, appended after s1. Left unchanged.
  allocator - Allocator used to provision the returned string's buffer.

Returns:
  A newly-allocated string containing self followed by s1 followed by s2.

The returned string owns its buffer and must be released via free_string
using the same allocator.
items.summary: Joins the string with two others, producing a newly-allocated result.

items.name: starts_with
items.comment:
Reports whether the string's first byte matches the given character.

Parameters:
  self - Pointer to the string to test.
  c    - Character to compare against the first byte of self.

Returns:
  true if self's leading byte equals c; false otherwise.
items.summary: Reports whether the string's first byte matches the given character.

items.name: starts_with
items.comment:
Reports whether the string begins with the given prefix.

Parameters:
  self - Pointer to the string to test.
  s1   - Candidate prefix to match against the start of self.

Returns:
  true if s1 is a prefix of self; false otherwise. Returns false when
  s1.length is greater than self.length. Equal-length strings match
  when their contents are identical.
items.summary: Reports whether the string begins with the given prefix.

items.name: get_hash
items.comment:
Produces a 64-bit hash for a string key by hashing each byte in order.

Parameters:
  x : string - string value to hash. Null or empty strings hash to the
               initial seed value.

Returns:
  u64 - hash value suitable for Map slot selection.

Notes:
  - This is a DJB2-style byte hash chosen because the current integer
    literal parser cannot represent the standard 64-bit FNV offset literal.
items.summary: Produces a 64-bit hash for a string key by hashing each byte in order.

items.name: Thread
items.comment:
Lightweight cross-platform thread handle.

Notes:
  - The native handle is platform-owned and should be treated as opaque.
  - A non-null native_handle means the Thread currently represents a
    joinable or detachable native thread.
items.summary: Lightweight cross-platform thread handle.

items.name: Thread
items.comment:
Creates and starts a new thread with the given entry point and user data.

Parameters:
  entry : ThreadFunc - function executed by the new thread.
  data  : ^void      - opaque pointer passed to entry.

Returns:
  [Thread, ThreadingStatus]
    - On success: the started Thread and ThreadingStatus.Ok.
    - On failure: an empty Thread and the platform start error.

Notes:
  - The returned thread should be joined or detached by the caller.
  - The data pointer must remain valid for as long as the thread may read it.
items.summary: Creates and starts a new thread with the given entry point and user data.

items.name: Thread
items.comment:
Creates an empty thread handle without starting a native thread.

Returns:
  Thread - handle whose native_handle is null.

Notes:
  - Use Thread.start to start it later.
items.summary: Creates an empty thread handle without starting a native thread.

items.name: get_current_thread
items.comment:
Returns a Thread handle representing the calling thread.

Returns:
  Thread - platform-specific handle for the current thread.

Notes:
  - This does not create a new thread.
  - Ownership semantics are platform-specific; do not destroy this as if it
    were created by Thread(entry, data).
items.summary: Returns a Thread handle representing the calling thread.

items.name: yield
items.comment: Gives the scheduler a chance to run another ready thread.
items.summary: Gives the scheduler a chance to run another ready thread.

items.name: start
items.signature: start : func(self : ^Thread, entry : ThreadFunc, data : ^void) -> [bool, ThreadingStatus]
items.comment:
Starts this thread handle with the given entry point and user data.

Parameters:
  self  : ^Thread    - thread handle to initialize.
  entry : ThreadFunc - function executed by the new native thread.
  data  : ^void      - opaque pointer passed to entry.

Returns:
  [bool, ThreadingStatus]
    - true and ThreadingStatus.Ok when the native thread was started.
    - false and an error status when self is invalid or already started.

Notes:
  - A thread can only be started once.
  - The caller should join or detach the thread after a successful start.
items.summary: Starts this thread handle with the given entry point and user data.

items.name: join
items.comment:
Waits for this thread to finish and optionally retrieves its return value.

Parameters:
  self      : ^Thread - thread to wait for.
  ret_value : ^^void  - optional output pointer for the thread result.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok on success, or a platform join error.

Notes:
  - Joining consumes the native handle; the Thread becomes invalid for
    future join/detach operations.
  - ret_value may be null if the caller does not need the thread result.
items.summary: Waits for this thread to finish and optionally retrieves its return value.

items.name: is_valid
items.comment: Returns true when this handle currently represents a native thread.
items.summary: Returns true when this handle currently represents a native thread.

items.name: detach
items.comment:
Releases this thread handle without waiting for the thread to finish.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok on success, or a platform detach error.

Notes:
  - Detaching consumes the native handle; the Thread becomes invalid for
    future join/detach operations.
  - The detached thread continues running independently.
items.summary: Releases this thread handle without waiting for the thread to finish.

items.name: exit
items.comment:
Exits the current running thread with an optional raw return value.

Parameters:
  self      : ^Thread - unused receiver; the current thread exits.
  ret_value : RawPtr  - value made available to a joining thread.

Returns:
  This function does not return on platforms where thread exit succeeds.

Notes:
  - The value should be null or point to memory that remains valid after
    this thread exits.
  - This exits the calling thread, not an arbitrary thread represented by
    self.
items.summary: Exits the current running thread with an optional raw return value.

items.name: Mutex
items.comment:
Lightweight cross-platform mutex handle.

Notes:
  - Use the platform Mutex() constructor to initialize it before locking.
  - initialized tracks whether the native mutex has been created.
items.summary: Lightweight cross-platform mutex handle.

items.name: destroy
items.comment:
Releases the native mutex resources.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok on success, or a platform destroy error.
items.summary: Releases the native mutex resources.

items.name: lock
items.comment:
Blocks until the mutex is acquired.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok on success, or a platform lock error.
items.summary: Blocks until the mutex is acquired.

items.name: try_lock
items.comment:
Attempts to acquire the mutex without blocking.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok when acquired, or ThreadingStatus.TryLockFailed when
  the mutex could not be acquired immediately.
items.summary: Attempts to acquire the mutex without blocking.

items.name: unlock
items.comment:
Releases a mutex previously acquired by this thread.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok on success, or a platform unlock error.
items.summary: Releases a mutex previously acquired by this thread.

items.name: CondVar
items.comment:
Lightweight cross-platform condition variable handle.

Notes:
  - Use the platform CondVar() constructor to initialize it before waiting or
    signaling.
  - A condition variable must be used together with a locked Mutex.
  - wait(mutex) atomically unlocks the mutex and puts the current thread to
    sleep. When the thread wakes, wait locks the mutex again before returning.
  - Always wait in a loop that checks shared state; wakeups can be spurious or
    another thread may consume the condition first.

Example:
  mutex := Mutex()
  cond := CondVar()
  ready := false

  // Waiting thread:
  mutex.lock()
  for (!ready) {
      cond.wait(&mutex)
  }
  mutex.unlock()

  // Signaling thread:
  mutex.lock()
  ready = true
  cond.signal()
  mutex.unlock()
items.summary: Lightweight cross-platform condition variable handle.

items.name: CondVar
items.comment:
Creates a condition variable and returns the handle directly.

Returns:
  CondVar - initialized on success, empty on failure.
items.summary: Creates a condition variable and returns the handle directly.

items.name: CondVar
items.comment:
Creates a condition variable and returns the handle directly.

Parameters:
  status : ^ThreadingStatus - optional output for initialization status.

Returns:
  CondVar - initialized on success, empty on failure.
items.summary: Creates a condition variable and returns the handle directly.

items.name: destroy
items.comment:
Releases the native condition variable resources.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok on success, or a platform destroy error.
items.summary: Releases the native condition variable resources.

items.name: wait
items.comment:
Atomically releases the mutex and waits until this condition variable is
signaled, then reacquires the mutex before returning.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok on success, or a platform wait error.

Notes:
  - The mutex must be locked by the calling thread before wait is called.
  - Callers should re-check their predicate after wait returns.
items.summary: Atomically releases the mutex and waits until this condition variable is signaled, then reacquires the mutex before returning.

items.name: signal
items.comment:
Wakes one thread waiting on this condition variable.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok on success, or a platform signal error.
items.summary: Wakes one thread waiting on this condition variable.

items.name: broadcast
items.comment:
Wakes all threads waiting on this condition variable.

Returns:
  ThreadingStatus.Ok on success, or a platform broadcast error.
items.summary: Wakes all threads waiting on this condition variable.
